Rob Edwards got off to a winning start as captain Dael Fry’s header settled our opening day clash with Swansea City.

It was a deserved victory for a determined Boro, who were gutsy and committed throughout against a resolute Swans side.

Fry scored what proved to be the winner seven minutes into the second half as we recorded back-to-back opening weekend victories over the Welsh outfit.

The game started in cagey fashion, although Boro were the more dominant team in possession.

The high press instigated by Edwards was in evidence, and a turnover forced by Tommy Conway led to a strike from Hayden Hackney which went wide.

Swansea went close twice in a two-minute spell, with Ronald’s sweet effort from distance skimming the side netting and Liam Cullen forcing Sol Brynn into a save from a header.

But Boro looked the more likely in the first half, and almost took the lead when Morgan Whittaker’s fierce drive was tipped onto the bar by Lawrence Vigouroux.

The Swansea goalkeeper was beaten from the resulting corner by Fry, but his header did not have enough on it. Boro kept the play alive and Delano Burgzorg saw an effort blocked.

The pattern continued into the second half, and our reward came on 52 minutes.

Whittaker whipped in a corner from the right and found the run of Fry, who continued his prolific form from pre-season with a terrific header into the bottom corner.

Visibly lifted by the goal, Boro went in search of more and could have had another when Hackney let fly from 20 yards, but his strike was deflected wide.

There was an impressive debut from the bench by Abdoulaye Kante as the Teessiders ground out the win, restricting any opportunities the visitors had to get back into the game.

Roared on by a Riverside crowd of more than 26,000, Boro got over the line to hand Edwards an excellent start.

He will hope to build on that on Tuesday when Doncaster Rovers visit in the first round of the Carabao Cup.

Boro were eliminated from the Carabao Cup at the first round stage as two early goals proved our undoing at the Riverside.

Doncaster Rovers inflicted the damage within the first 23 minutes with a pair of deflected strikes.

Rob Edwards’ side pushed for a route back into the tie but were unable to get on the scoresheet on a balmy Teesside night.

The away team then wrapped things up with two goals in the closing stages.

Doncaster took the lead on 11 minutes, with Ben Close’s strike from inside the area deflecting past Tom Glover.

There was almost an immediate response from Boro when Delano Burgzorg beat his man and smashed an effort which crashed against the post.

A tremendous one-handed save from Ian Lawlor then kept out Morgan Whittaker’s sweet hit, but Doncaster remained a threat themselves at the other end.

They doubled their advantage with another deflected effort midway through the first half, this time from Damola Ajayi.

It was almost three when Jordan Gibson headed into the side netting but Boro ended the half well, and went close to halving the deficit, but Burgzorg’s shot was tipped round the post by Lawlor.

Boro started the second half brightly and had two early sights of goal. Callum Brittain’s strike was kept out by Lawlor and a powerful drive from Whittaker whistled over the crossbar.

Lawlor was again Boro’s nemesis when he denied Whittaker with a fine save shortly afterwards.

Boro made a trio of changes just after the hour mark and one of those brought on, Hayden Hackney, almost made an immediate impact.

His attempt was blocked, though, as was the follow-up from Law McCabe, before McCabe's half volley narrowly cleared the crossbar.

Whittaker continued to provide a threat, slicing wide from distance and then having a free-kick saved, but Doncaster effectively sealed their win six minutes from the end through Robbie Gotts.

Tom Nixon found the bottom corner deep into stoppage time to complete the scoring.

Boro came away from the Lions’ Den with three points as Hayden Hackney and Alfie Jones' second half strikes saw off Millwall.

It was an outstanding victory for Rob Edwards’ men in the capital as they overcame a fast start from their hosts to secure a second straight league win.

Hackney’s effort on 49 minutes proved pivotal for the Teessiders, before Alfie Jones and Delano Burgzorg sealed the deal late on as we sent our terrific travelling support home in joyous mood.

There was one change to the Boro team which started on the opening day against Swansea City, with Abdoulaye Kante replacing Delano Burgzorg.

It was a first half of contrasts for the away side, who started on the back foot but ended strongly.

The Teessiders had to deal with some early Millwall pressure, although Sol Brynn was not overly tested.

He watched as a Camiel Neghli header sailed wide on 20 minutes, but Boro were growing into it by that stage.

We almost went in front when Sam Silvera’s cross from the left dropped into a perfect area, but Morgan Whittaker could only nudge it past the post.

The hosts thought they had scored on 41 minutes, but Casper De Norre’s powerful, goalbound low drive was brilliantly kept out by the outstretched leg of Luke Ayling.

There was a big talking point less than two minutes later when Tommy Conway was sent racing through and went down under a challenge from goalkeeper Steven Benda, but the referee ruled no foul had taken place and the teams went in at half-time level.

Sontje Hansen was introduced from the bench at the break as he came on for his Boro debut.

The Dutchman made an immediate impact as his smart turn and pass found Morgan Whittaker down the right and he in turn picked out Hackney, whose effort kissed the post on its way past Benda to give Boro the lead.

It was a pulsating start to the second half, and further goalmouth action followed at both ends.

Hackney was vital at the other end, blocking from Josh Coburn to set off a Boro counter attack which ended with a Callum Brittain strike which Benda did well to save.

The hosts could not have come much closer to equalising on 53 minutes when former Boro man Coburn’s header rebounded off both posts as Boro breathed a sigh of relief.

The frantic action calmed from there and we again began to threaten, with a Silvera shot deflecting onto the roof of the net and Jones firing wide from a corner.

Boro were edging closer to victory and almost sealed it 11 minutes from time, but substitute Finn Azaz's curler went narrowly over.

Jones added the finishing touch with three minutes left, though, firing into the roof of the net from a corner to cap off a superb away performance, before Burgzorg sealed it in stoppage time.

Azaz played a tremendous ball into the frontman and he took a touch before brilliantly beating Benda.

Brilliant Boro made it three wins from three with a superb away performance at Carrow Road.

Rob Edwards' side were rewarded for a positive first half with two quickfire goals in the closing stages of it, with Finn Azaz and Tommy Conway putting us in front.

Boro then limited Norwich's opportunities after half-time, and although the hosts pulled one back in the closing stages, we saw things out to continue our perfect start in the Sky Bet Championship.

Edwards made one change to the side which started the 3-0 win at Millwall a week earlier, with Azaz replacing Abdoulaye Kante.

There was almost a huge opportunity for a Boro opener within the first three minutes when we pounced on a loose touch from home goalkeeper Vladan Kovacevic, but Azaz and Morgan Whittaker could not quite bring it under control.

Boro’s press was earning some early dividends but Norwich were threatening on the break, and we needed captain Dael Fry to get across quickly to snuff out an opportunity for Jakov Medic.

The hosts wrestled some initiative as the half progressed, with Josh Sargent heading two decent chances wide and Papa Amadou Diallo also curling narrowly past the post.

But Boro continued to cause problems, and we could have taken the lead when Aidan Morris stole possession high up the pitch and beat the goalkeeper, only for his chip to clear the crossbar.

Moments later though, we were ahead.

Hayden Hackney carried the ball through the centre and laid it off to Azaz, who took a touch and slammed it past Kovacevic at his near post.

It became a quickfire double on 45 minutes when we won possession high again and Morris slid a perfect ball across the face of goal for Conway to tap home.

As Boro would have expected, Norwich came out strongly at the start of the second half and we needed a superb Luke Ayling block to deny Ante Crnac.

Sol Brynn was then called into action to thwart Diallo but we responded well, and could have gone further ahead.

Azaz's tremendous through ball found Conway and he sprinted towards goal, but Canaries defender Harry Darling reacted well and got back to block.

Norwich were reduced to 10 men before the hour when Jacob Wright tried to recover from a loose touch and lunged into Morris, catching the Boro midfielder on the leg.

The home side remained in contention, though, and fired a warning when Mirko Topic fired just wide from the edge of the box.

Sontje Hansen was brought on in the 67th minute and almost made an immediate impact, but he was denied by a fingertip save from Kovacevic.

There was no letting up from the Teessiders, with Ayling the next to have a go as his strike from distance was kept out by the legs of Kovacevic.

The real work was in continuing to keep Norwich at bay, though, and there was a late scare when Sargent chipped in with five minutes remaining.

However, we showed resolve to see things out and claim a third straight league victory.

Tommy Conway’s superb second half finish delivered a fourth win in a row for Boro as we got the better of Sheffield United at the Riverside.

Rob Edwards’ men had been unable to get their noses in front despite an impressive first half display, but Conway’s strike 19 minutes after the restart proved the difference.

It means the Teessiders’ 100% record remains intact heading into the international break.

There was one change to the team which started the 2-1 win at Norwich City, with Sontje Hansen making his first start for Boro.

We enjoyed much the better of the first half, largely dominating possession, territory and the chances which came.

There was almost an early opener when Sam Silvera cut onto his right foot and whipped a shot narrowly past the post, while a ball across the six-yard box from Aidan Morris narrowly evaded a decisive touch.

Silvera was caught late by Sydie Peck in a controversial moment which could have resulted in a red card for the Sheffield United man, but the referee opted to show the midfielder a yellow.

Japhet Tanganga blocked a goalbound strike from Callum Brittain, who also went close to providing a goal for Conway, who was just unable to connect with his dangerous cross.

Boro needed an outstanding, last-ditch tackle from Hayden Hackney on Louie Barry, though, in the closing stages of the first half to remain on level terms.

There was a testing start to the second half for Boro as the Blades showed signs of improvement, but Sol Brynn was not tested.

Edwards had made two changes at the break, with Matt Targett brought on for his debut and Sverre Nypan introduced for his first appearance at the Riverside.

Within 19 minutes of being brought on, Targett had his first goal involvement in a Boro shirt.

His superb ball down the left found Conway, who took it past a defender and produced a tremendous, unerring finish into the bottom corner to hand us the lead.

That was among Conway’s final contributions and was just reward for his selfless play leading the line.

He was replaced by Kaly Sene just a day after he had been confirmed as a Boro player, and the Senegalese forward produced several bright moments as we looked to make the points safe.

Sheffield United made a flurry of changes as they battled for a way back into the game and one of those brought on, Danny Ings, went close with a deflected effort which dropped just wide.

But Boro held firm and largely restricted their visitors to claim another richly deserved three points.

Boro rescued a point from a dramatic encounter at Deepdale after twice battling back from a goal behind.

Lewis Dobbin fired the hosts into a first half lead, and Preston proved difficult opponents to break down.

Rob Edwards’ men kept plugging away, and got their reward 18 minutes from the end as Matt Targett marked his first start for the club with a goal.

There was a sting in the tail as Jordan Storey headed in what looked like it may be the winner on 88 minutes.

We bundled in a stoppage time equaliser, though, as Sontje Hansen's goalbound effort bounced over the line to send the 5,600 away fans into raptures.

There were three changes to the Boro team which started the 1-0 win over Sheffield United before the international break.

Targett and Kaly Sene were brought in for their first starts, while Darragh Lenihan was named in a competitive starting XI for the first time since September 2023.

There were few chances in the early stages, but Preston went in front just before the midway point in the first half. Dobbin carried the ball to the edge of the box and picked out the top corner with a sweet strike.

Boro responded brightly and had an opportunity to level when Daniel Iversen punched a Targett corner as far as Luke Ayling, who volleyed over.

We were unable to turn dominance in possession into clear-cut openings, though, with Hayden Hackney’s stoppage time shot wide the only other real sight of goal in the first half.

David Strelec was brought on for his Boro debut at half-time and the Slovakian made an immediate impact.

Boro’s start to the second half was excellent, with Strelec having an early shot deflected wide and Callum Brittain denied by the offside flag after he fired in from close range.

Preston continued to be difficult to break down but we got back on level terms with 18 minutes remaining, thanks in large part down to some outstanding work from substitute Sverre Nypan.

After some silky footwork saw him force his way past a defender, he slide a ball across the area which Tommy Conway was not quite able to convert. It broke away to Targett, though, whose right foot volley nestled in the bottom corner to spark wild scenes in the packed away end.

Edwards' side pushed for what they hopes would be a winner, but a cruel blow came at the other end as Storey headed in from a corner late on.

Alan Browne had a goalbound effort blocked in stoppage time against his former club, and from the resulting corner, there was more drama.

Strelec had a strike saved on the line and Hansen's shot bounced towards goal before the ball was bundled over the line by Browne on his debut, although it was initially unclear whether the midfielder had got a touch.

It was a fitting end to a dramatic second half as we kept our unbeaten record alive.

David Strelec and Kaly Sene fired Boro to a fifth win from six as they netted their first goals for the club on a raucous night at the Riverside.

Slovakian striker Strelec marked his first start for the club by firing us into a first half lead which Sene doubled after being brought on at the break.

West Brom pulled one back in the closing stages but there was no way back for the Baggies as we made it our best-ever start to a league season.

Alongside Strelec, Sverre Nypan also made his first start for Boro, while George Edmundson was in the XI for the first time this season.

All three were in the thick of the action in the first half, although it was the visitors who had the first sight of goal when Nat Phillips forced Sol Brynn into a save with his legs.

The brightest play in the opening 45 came from Boro, with Strelec and Nypan combining to create the first opportunity, which Nypan drilled wide from the edge of the area.

Tommy Conway also went close when he wriggled free down the left of the box and drew a sharp save from Josh Griffiths at his near post.

Boro’s breakthrough came from a new source on 26 minutes.

Edmundson’s long throw from the left was flicked on by Luke Ayling and prodded home from inside the six-yard box by Strelec as the Slovakian marked his home debut in style.

There was a blow late in the first half for Boro as Edmundson was forced off with an injury to his eye, but we maintained our lead into the interval.

Another change came at half-time as Strelec was replaced by fellow summer arrival Sene.

West Brom started the second half well, and a presentable opportunity was headed wide by Isaac Price within two minutes of the restart.

Jed Wallace also fired past the post and Alex Mowatt struck one over from range as the visitors enjoyed their best spell.

Our response was emphatic, though, with Nypan stinging the palms of Griffiths with a left-foot piledriver from range.

Brynn had to be sharp to keep out a low strike from Ousmane Diakite and what seemed like moments later, the save took on even greater significance.

Neat footwork from Conway opened up some space in the West Brom box and when his ball was flicked by Hayden Hackney to Sene, the substitute rifled us further ahead with an unerring effort into the bottom corner.

The Baggies made it a nervy ending when Aune Heggebo halved our lead with a header on 90 minutes, but we saw out five minutes of stoppage time to record a third straight home victory.

Kaly Sene kept Boro's unbeaten start to the season intact as his late equaliser earned us a share of the spoils at St Mary's.

It had looked as though we may taste defeat for the first time when Adam Armstrong fired Southampton into the lead just after the hour mark.

Substitute Sene struck home 12 minutes before the end, though, as Rob Edwards' side again displayed their battling qualities and never-say-die spirit.

There was one change to the Boro team which started the 2-1 win over West Bromwich Albion, with Morgan Whittaker replacing Sverre Nypan in the XI.

The hosts started well and created an opening which Ross Stewart struck against the legs of Luke Ayling.

It was Boro enjoying the better of the early possession, though, and we almost took the lead just after the quarter-hour when Matt Targett bent a free-kick around the wall and was denied by the post.

Home left-back Ryan Manning curled a similar free-kick wide at the other end and later inadvertently set up a chance for Finn Azaz when his strike deflected into his path, but the Irish international could only hook the ball over.

Clear-cut opportunities were scarce, although we had a sight of goal when David Strelec did well to find Tommy Conway and he had two efforts, the first of which was blocked before he fired the follow-up into the side netting.

The Saints were frustrated two minutes into stoppage time as Joshua Quarshie’s header from a corner bounced up and over the bar.

Boro enjoyed a strong spell at the start of the second half as we began to put our hosts under pressure.

A Targett free-kick fell to Conway, who skewed a shot wide.

There was later a chance when a well-worked move down the right found Whittaker and he in turn played it to Strelec, whose strike was deflected against the post.

There was a hammer blow at the other end just after the hour, though, as a right-wing cross found its way to Armstrong and he clinically drilled it left-footed into the bottom corner.

Our unbeaten start to the season was under threat, but the Teessiders did not back down.

We drew back on level terms in superb style on 78 minutes when Ayling's tremendous ball down the right found substitute Kaly Sene and he thundered a shot which hit a defender, then the crossbar and then the back of the net to send the travelling support into raptures.

A superb Alfie Jones block kept us on level terms moments later as the home side looked for an immediate response.

Both teams posed an attacking threat in the closing stages and maximum points could have gone in either direction, but the spoils were ultimately shared.

Two of the Sky Bet Championship's top three played out a goalless draw on a night of fine margins at the Riverside.

Both teams had strong attacking spells they were unable to take advantage of, with Boro particularly strong in the first half.

The deadlock could not be broken at either end, though, with Rob Edwards' side adding another point to their tally to continue their unbeaten start.

There were two changes to the Boro team which started Saturday’s draw at Southampton, with Sverre Nypan and Alan Browne replacing Callum Brittain and Morgan Whittaker.

We were forced into an early substitution when George Edmundson was withdrawn within the first seven minutes. Sam Silvera came on in his place.

Within moments of that, we almost went in front as Hayden Hackney strode through the centre of the park and unleashed a 20-yard drive which Viktor Johansson did well to palm wide.

Johansson pulled off another fine save to deny David Strelec, whose effort was destined for the top corner, and also kept out a low shot from Aidan Morris.

There was controversy just after the half-hour when Tommy Conway went down under a challenge in the penalty area, but the referee waved away the strong appeals and booked the Boro striker.

A sense of frustration lingered for the remainder of the half as Boro continued to dominate possession, but Stoke proved difficult to break down.

Stoke started the second half strongly and Sol Brynn was forced into an early save, springing to his left to claw away a curler from Sorba Thomas.

There was almost immediately an opening at the other end as Hackney teed up Aidan Morris 12 yards out, but the American’s strike comfortably cleared the crossbar.

It was the Potters doing much of the early attacking as they enjoyed their brightest spell, but our threat continued too, and a Strelec strike was deflected over after a dangerous counter.

The game became stretched and both sides looked capable of breaking the deadlock.

A double change from Boro injected some further attacking impetus and one of those introduced, Sontje Hansen, flashed a ball across the face of goal which went narrowly past the far post.

At the other end, Sol Brynn was forced to make a tremendous save with his foot to deny Tomas Rigo after space opened up in the area for the Stoke substitute.

Johansson then pulled off a tremendous fingertip stop from Hansen, whose rocket was arrowing for the roof of the net, and at that point it looked destined to end goalless.

Brynn made a fine save from Divin Mubama in stoppage time and that was that as the teams took a point apiece.

Boro tasted defeat for the first time in the league this season at Fratton Park.

Minhyeok Yang handed Portsmouth the lead midway through the first half and despite much Boro pushing, there would be no equaliser.

The result means we head into the second international break of the campaign in second place and on 18 points.

Callum Brittain, Dael Fry, Kaly Sene and Sontje Hansen were restored to the Boro line-up by Rob Edwards, replacing George Edmundson, Alan Browne, Sverre Nypan and David Strelec.

The Teessiders had a promising start to the game, with two dangerous attacks leading to strikes from the edge of the box from Aidan Morris and Hayden Hackney. Hackney went closest, with his effort deflected wide.

Pompey began to hit back and almost scored when Conor Chaplin’s shot from near the penalty spot was brilliantly blocked by Alfie Jones, who diverted it just past the post.

The home side did take the lead in the 23rd minute, with Jordan Williams’ cross from the right struck sweetly home by Tottenham Hotspur loanee Minhyeok.

There was little in the way of goalmouth action in the remainder of the first 45 minutes as Pompey carried their advantage into the break.

Boro survived an early scare in the second half when, less than a minute after the restart, Chaplin’s sweet strike from distance went narrowly wide.

Our start to the half was strong after that, and a period of relative pressure led to a superb Matt Targett cross which found Sontje Hansen, whose effort was off target.

There was also an opening when Tommy Conway’s shot was deflected into the path of Morris, but he could only skew it wide.

Callum Brittain was the next to have a sighter when he was picked out by Targett, but he was crowded out and the ball squirted into the hands of home goalkeeper Josef Bursik.

Portsmouth were able to stem the tide of Boro attacks, although we did look the likelier team to score in the remainder of the game.

The closest Boro came to a leveller was in the 83rd minute as Targett's strike took a deflection and almost led to a tap-in for substitute Strelec, but he was not quite able to stretch enough to turn it home.

We are back in action after the international break when we take on Ipswich Town at the Riverside.

Boro returned to winning ways in superb fashion at the Riverside.

An energetic and dynamic display produced maximum points against Ipswich Town on a dramatic Friday night on Teesside.

A breathless first half reached its climax as Sol Brynn pulled off a stunning penalty save before an own goal at the other end handed us the advantage.

Morgan Whittaker fired home his first goal for Boro 10 minutes into the second half and that proved to be enough for Rob Edwards' men to return to the top of the table, despite Ipswich pulling one back in the final quarter-hour.

Delano Burgzorg, Whittaker, David Strelec and Alan Browne were brought into the starting XI by Edwards as we returned to action following the international break.

Boro had two decent attempts in the first half-hour, both of which were from Hayden Hackney, while blocks from Dael Fry and Alfie Jones respectively denied Sam Szmodics and George Hirst at the other end.

That was a relatively serene opening compared to the action-packed final 10 minutes of the first half which followed.

Ipswich goalkeeper Alex Palmer was a thorn in Boro’s side, keeping out a one-on-one effort from Tommy Conway and also producing a tremendous save from Hackney.

Palmer then brilliantly denied Browne before there was an even better save by Fry as Ipswich offered a threat of their own, with the Boro captain acrobatically keeping out Szmodics’ header.

There was another big chance for the hosts when Burgzorg stung Palmer’s hands and David Strelec hit the rebound wide.

That looked set to be a vital moment when Callum Brittain was adjudged to have fouled Leif Davis in the box. However, Brynn sprung brilliantly to his right to push Hirst’s penalty around the post and keep the scores level.

It got even better for Boro in stoppage time. Burgzorg burst away down the right of the area and his ball across the area confused Ipswich defender Cedric Kipre enough for him to turn the ball in his own net.

That capped a dramatic end to the half as we went in at the break with the lead.

The second half had much to live up to and from a Boro perspective, it could not have started much better.

Hackney had a shot blocked and Whittaker fired over within six minutes of the restart as we looked to press home our advantage.

The vital second goal arrived on 55 minutes as Strelec's low ball from the right was parried by Palmer to Whittaker, who drilled home to score his first goal for the club.

Whittaker had produced an excellent performance and had a sight of goal again soon afterwards, but his strike from the right of the area drifted wide.

Dara O'Shea gave Ipswich hope when he headed in from a corner with 14 minutes remaining.

That prompted a nervy ending, and a strong hand from Brynn diverted a dangerous Jack Clarke cross to safety.

There was to be no late drama, though, as Boro saw it out to claim maximum points.

Boro got the better of a spirited Sheffield Wednesday side to make it back-to-back wins.

Morgan Whittaker handed Rob Edwards' side a fifth-minute lead at Hillsborough with a placed finish from inside the area.

There were several opportunities for that advantage to be extended, but Wednesday refused to lie down and kept the result in doubt until the closing stages.

The Teessiders held firm to claim a third away victory of the season ahead of Saturday's meeting with Wrexham at the Riverside.

Boro were unchanged from the 2-1 win over Ipswich Town and dominated the first half at Hillsborough.

It took just five minutes for Whittaker to open the scoring as he swept home a low Delano Burgzorg cross to make it two goals in as many games. It followed some fine work from Alan Browne and Matt Targett in the build-up.

Whittaker had another effort deflected wide and Tommy Conway hit one past the post after another superb ball from Burgzorg.

There was controversy when Conway beat Joe Lumley to the ball and appeared to be scythed down by the Wednesday goalkeeper, with the referee waving away Boro’s penalty appeals.

The Teessiders continued to create openings in the remainder of the half, but there was to be no second goal before the break.

Hayden Hackney curled wide from the edge of the area and Lumley denied both Conway and Burgzorg in the closing stages.

After being little more than a spectator in the first 45 minutes, Sol Brynn became a central character at the start of the second half.

He did brilliantly to claw a deflected Dominic Iorfa header to safety and then pushed a sweet Svante Ingelsson strike around the post.

The home side had come out of the blocks strongly after half-time but Boro emerged from their initial burst unscathed and set about extending the lead.

They came up against an inspired goalkeeping performance from former Boro goalkeeper Lumley, though.

He beat away a Whittaker strike, saved from Conway from point-blank range and then produced the save of the lot, with his tremendous fingertip stop denying Browne.

Browne and Burgzorg both fired into the side netting as we maintained the pressure, and the Irishman was frustrated again when his sweetly-struck half volley was deflected wide.

Boro could not quite get that second goal to settle any nerves - with Kaly Sene the final player to be denied by Lumley in stoppage time - but it was ultimately not required.

Hayden Hackney salvaged Boro's unbeaten home record in the league with a late header.

An early deflected strike looked like it may be enough for the Welsh side on their first visit to the Riverside.

Hackney headed home with 10 minutes to play to snuff that out and although Rob Edwards' side pushed for a winner, it ended with a point apiece.

Aidan Morris, Sverre Nypan and Kaly Sene were brought into the starting XI but it was a difficult opening 45 minutes for Boro.

Ryan Longman tested Sol Brynn with an effort from range and from the resulting corner, Wrexham took the lead.

The ball was played short to Josh Windass and his strike took two deflections on its way past Brynn with just seven minutes on the clock.

Boro dominated possession in the remainder of the half but were limited to shots from distance, with Hayden Hackney and Morris both curling over.

Alfie Jones made a vital block from Windass at the other end but there were to be no further goals before the break.

Edwards made four changes at the break and Boro were quickly on the front foot, although Wrexham remained tough to break down.

There were two half-openings for Kaly Sene, although he was unable to get a clean shot off on either occasion, while half-time introduction Tommy Conway forced Arthur Okonkwo into his first save.

We were unable to carve out regular opportunities, though, and breathed a sigh of relief at the other end when Kieffer Moore's header hit the top of the crossbar.

Boro's frustration was ended with 10 minutes remaining as Callum Brittain's cross from the right found Hackney and he powered in a header at the far post.

Hackney eyed a quickfire double to turn the game on its head, but his free-kick was kept out by Okonkwo.

Luke Ayling thought he had found the winner in the 89th minute, only for Okonkwo to claw his tremendous strike over the bar.

Boro pushed for another goal through four minutes of stoppage time, but Wrexham held on to claim a draw.

Boro fell to a 3-0 defeat on a difficult afternoon at Vicarage Road.

After going behind on 15 minutes, Rob Edwards' side responded well, but were unable to find an equaliser.

The crucial second goal went the way of the hosts just after the half-hour and they added a third early in the second half to seal the points.

It was just a second league loss of the season for the Teessiders.

There were three changes to the Boro starting line-up, with Luke Ayling, Alan Browne and Tommy Conway brought into the XI.

The Teessiders made a bright start, with Conway and Hayden Hackney both having sights of goal, but Watford opened the scoring on 15 minutes.

Boro were outnumbered on the counter as Kwadwo Baah blazed down the right flank. He pulled a ball back across the area, where Hornets captain Imran Louza was on hand to strike home.

We made a decent response, and almost drew level when Matt Targett’s free-kick was tipped over by Egil Selvik as it headed for the top corner.

Watford hit Boro with a sucker-punch just after the half-hour as Jeremy Ngakia’s cross from deep was met with a terrific one-touch finish from Luca Kjerrumgaard.

Boro’s task was made even harder four minutes into the second half when Mamadou Doumbia found the net with a sweet strike from distance. The ball appeared to hit an offside Kjerrumgaard on its way in, but the goal stood.

Delano Burgzorg attempted to reduce the arrears with a 20-yard shot which whistled wide, and Conway also went close, with his goalbound effort blocked by Mattie Pollock.

Substitute David Strelec was unfortunate not to score in stoppage time, with his strike going just past the post before he later had a header tipped over, but the damage had already been done.

Boro will aim to bounce back in Tuesday's trip to Leicester City.

Luke Ayling's brilliant header sealed a dramatic point for Boro at the King Power.

Trailing 1-0 and with a man fewer on the pitch, Ayling rose to head home six minutes into stoppage time for Rob Edwards' men.

We had fallen behind to a penalty deep into first half stoppage time, and defeat looked likely when Alfie Jones was sent off on 90 minutes.

Ayling had other ideas, though, as he towered home at the death to clinch a share of the spoils.

Morgan Whittaker and David Strelec were brought into the Boro line-up in place of Dael Fry and Alan Browne, who started the 3-0 loss at Watford.

It proved to be a frustrating first half for the Teessiders, who were dominant in possession but found it difficult to create openings, and went in at half-time behind.

The best opportunities of the opening 45 minutes fell to Leicester.

Abdul Fatawu headed wide at the back post, Caleb Okoli was off target from close range and Julian Carranza fired past the post from a free-kick.

Boro’s best chance came when Matt Targett stung the palms of Jakub Stolarczyk with a 20-yard strike. The Leicester goalkeeper picked himself up to also deny Strelec on the rebound.

It looked set to be a goalless first half until Leicester were awarded a penalty deep into stoppage time, with Hayden Hackney adjudged to have handled in the area.

Jordan Ayew took the responsibility from the spot and rolled the ball home to put the Foxes in front.

There was an early chance for Boro in the second half when Targett’s cross to the back post found Callum Brittain, but he miscued his volley and it went wide.

Morgan Whittaker went close soon after when his whipped effort flashed onto the roof of the net as we continued to attack with vigour.

A breakthrough was not forthcoming, though, as Leicester stabilised.

Riley McGree and Sverre Nypan were the first players introduced from the bench and both made positive impacts to give Boro renewed threat.

Nypan almost created the equaliser, but his low cross was turned just past his own post by Ben Nelson.

Tommy Conway saw a penalty appeal waved away and sent a header wide, while Whittaker's 25-yard strike went through a sea of bodies but was nudged just off target.

Conway's eyes lit up when the ball broke to him in the box with three minutes left, only for substitute goalkeeper Asmir Begovic to make a superb reflex save. Boro kept it alive and McGree curled narrowly wide just seconds later.

Leicester had dropped deeper the longer the second half went on, but Boro looked headed for defeat when Jones was sent off on 90 minutes.

There was one dramatic twist to come, though, as Ayling rose to head home a Brittain cross five minutes into added time to seal a point.

We will aim to return to winning ways when Birmingham City visit the Riverside on Saturday.

Boro personified the spirit of Teesside as goals from Dael Fry and Hayden Hackney sealed a brilliant win over Birmingham City at the Riverside.

Fry put us in front from a corner early on, but the visitors equalised just before the half hour in contentious circumstances to half our momentum.

Hayden Hackney's expert flick six minutes into first half stoppage time restored Boro's advantage, and the Teessiders were forced to show plenty of resilience after the break to seal the points.

Do that they did in front of a superb, vocal home support as we signed off for the international break in winning fashion.

Riley McGree was handed his first start of the season and he was one of three Boro changes, with Dael Fry and Alan Browne also brought into the XI.

A lively atmosphere awaited the teams and Boro started on the front foot, with McGree particularly influential. He drilled wide early on.

Tomoki Iwata flashed a shot beyond the post at the other end but it was Boro making most of the inroads, with Browne stinging the palms of goalkeeper James Beadle as we fired another warning.

The breakthrough came on 17 minutes as Fry demonstrated the spirit of Teesside to put us in front. Callum Brittain’s in-swinger from the right was met by the determination of Fry in the six-yard box as he got in front of his man to nudge us into the lead. It was a third assist in four games for Brittain.

Birmingham responded well and we needed a superb block from Luke Ayling to keep us level before Fry was forced off with an injury in the 26th minute.

Sol Brynn superbly denied Patrick Roberts but the Blues’ leveller came shortly afterwards, with Demarai Gray finishing from close range after the referee ruled he had not pushed Sam Silvera in the back.

Silvera tested Beadle from distance in the second of seven minutes of stoppage time as we ended the half back on top.

Boro’s reward came with one minute of added time remaining as Aidan Morris’ strike from range was brilliantly flicked home by Hackney to send the South Stand into raptures.

Brynn made a fine save from Jay Stansfield early in a second half which was mainly devoid of clear-cut opportunities.

Boro had to show plenty of resilience to restrict their visitors, and Brynn needed to be sharp to save from Roberts with 13 minutes left.

A makeshift back five of Silvera, George McCormick, Luke Ayling, Browne and Brittain did superbly to get us over the line.

It was a day when collective effort was paramount as we returned to second spot.

Boro return to action after the international break with a trip to Oxford United.

Morgan Whittaker’s second half strike earned Boro a point at Oxford United.

Whittaker levelled the scores nine minutes into the second half, cancelling out Luke Harris’ 27th-minute opener for the home side.

Boro pushed for a winner on an afternoon which saw them control most of the game, but it was not forthcoming.

There were two changes to the Boro team which started the 2-1 win over Birmingham City a fortnight earlier, with Alfie Jones and Delano Burgzorg introduced in place of Dael Fry and Riley McGree.

We started well and Callum Brittain had our first sight of goal, but his left foot effort lacked the power needed to seriously trouble the hosts.

Aidan Morris’ sweet strike from range whistled just over the bar as Boro looked to make their dominance in possession count, but we were to be stung at the other end.

Against the run of play, Oxford took the lead on 27 minutes. Jack Currie’s low ball from the left was met by a thumping finish from Luke Harris, who picked out the bottom corner.

Boro’s time on the ball increased further after the goal, but an equaliser proved elusive in the first half.

Morgan Whittaker had a low strike saved by Jamie Cumming and another one blocked, as did Tommy Conway in stoppage time as Oxford retained their advantage into the interval.

Boro’s aggression in the press was evident from the first whistle in the second half, and we had an early chance when Brittain stung the palms of Cumming.

The right-back was heavily involved in our equaliser on 54 minutes. Morris found him down the right of the area, and his fine low ball into the danger zone was stroked home by Whittaker.

Adi Viveash made tweaks as the second half progressed as Boro looked to prise another opening, but Oxford proved difficult to break down.

Whittaker was inches away from a stunning second as his shot from 20 yards flew past the upright, and that was as close as we came to a winner.

We are back in action on Tuesday when Coventry City visit the Riverside.

Boro suffered a late blow as Coventry City became the first visiting side to win at the Riverside in league action this season.

After falling behind to two goals inside the first 14 minutes, we battled back in a pulsating game.

Morgan Whittaker pulled one back just after the half-hour and we got back on level terms early in the second half through an own goal.

There were chances for Boro to win it as the game ebbed and flowed, but two goals inside the final five minutes sealed the points for Coventry.

With new head coach Kim Hellberg watching from the stands, Adi Viveash made two changes to the Boro team which started Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Oxford United. Sam Silvera and Riley McGree were the men brought in, replacing Matt Targett and Delano Burgzorg in the XI.

An exciting first half which featured plenty of action at both ends started with Boro on top.

Whittaker saw a cross scrambled to safety, Silvera fired over and Whittaker had a goalbound strike deflected narrowly wide.

We fell behind against the run of play on 10 minutes, though, as Coventry won the ball centrally and played it through to Ellis Simms, whose effort from the left of the area looped into the top corner.

The Sky Blues made it a quickfire double when Matt Grimes’ superb cross was headed in by Liam Kitching.

It could have been three when Simms raced through looking for his brace, but Luke Ayling tracked him well and made a superbly timed challenge to deny him.

Boro survived a difficult spell without falling further behind, and spiritedly battled back into the game as we began to make our dominance in possession count.

Whittaker halved the deficit just after the half hour. Alan Browne’s cross from the right of the box was flicked on by Alfie Jones and volleyed in by the forward for his second goal in as many games.

We breathed a sigh of relief at the other end when Josh Eccles’ header dropped just wide.

It was Boro with the initiative, though, and an equaliser almost came via the left foot of McGree, but his half volley was headed over his own net by Kitching.

Boro were forced into a half-time change, with Targett replacing the injured Aidan Morris.

Sol Brynn was called into action within 20 seconds of the restart, pulling off an outstanding one-handed save to deny Simms his second of the night.

We quickly found our feet again, and almost drew back on level terms when Whittaker’s terrific strike was tipped over by Carl Rushworth.

The resulting corner did produce the equaliser, though, as Bobby Thomas’ sliced clearance from Hayden Hackney’s corner went into his own net in front of the North Stand.

With the wind in our sails, Boro threatened to take the lead for the first time, but Coventry stemmed the tide to make it a tighter second half.

The visitors had a chance to restore their lead with 20 minutes remaining, only for Grimes’ strike to cannon against his team-mate Tatsuhiro Sakamoto as it arrowed towards goal.

There was a big chance for Boro to go in front when Callum Brittain’s ball across goal found Tommy Conway, but his effort went over the top.

The crucial fifth goal of the game went to Coventry with five minutes remaining, with Brynn making a superb save with his foot from Thomas before the ball cannoned against Kitching and into the net.

Simms headed in shortly afterwards to seal the win for the Sky Blues.

We return to action at the Riverside on Saturday as Hellberg takes charge of his first game, against Derby County.

Boro came from behind with two goals in the final 15 minutes to win Kim Hellberg’s first game in charge on a dramatic afternoon at a sodden Riverside.

Derby County took the lead inside the first two minutes before Boro went on to dominate the ball, creating several opportunities for an equaliser.

It took until a 75th minute Matt Targett header to draw back on level terms, and Morgan Whittaker won it against his former club with six minutes left.

Hellberg made three changes from the side which started our midweek loss to Derby County, with Targett, Alex Bangura and Sontje Hansen brought into the XI.

We found ourselves behind within two minutes, with Lars-Jorgen Salvesen’s flick finding Patrick Agyemang, who drilled it into the bottom corner.

Boro’s response was decent, with Whittaker having a strike deflected wide and Targett seeing a free-kick saved, but Derby remained a threat at the other end, particularly through Agyemang.

The USA international fired another opportunity over and was denied by a fine Alfie Jones tackle, before further vital interventions from Targett and Sol Brynn kept the deficit at one.

Boro were dominant in possession and as the first half progressed, began to turn that into chances for an equaliser.

Bangura – making his first appearance of the season – was prominent down the left flank, and a dangerous cross from him was scrambled to safety.

We went agonisingly close on 35 minutes when Callum Brittain’s left-foot shot struck the crossbar and then the goalline, before bouncing away from the target.

Delano Burgzorg hooked a decent chance over but the Derby goal remained unbreached.

Matt Clarke and Salvesen both had sights of goal from set-pieces in the closing stages of the half, but the score remained 1-0 to the visitors at the interval.

Boro came out strongly at the start of the second half and saw a strong penalty appeal turned down when Burgzorg’s strike was charged down by Clarke, with the officials waving away our appeals for handball.

Hayden Hackney went close with a curler from the edge of the box and Targett went closer still, with his free-kick arrowing inches past the upright.

Derby stemmed the flow of Boro attacks but we kept probing, and fired a warning to the visitors when Whittaker’s free-kick was tipped wide by Jacob Widell Zetterstrom.

Another Boro penalty appeal was turned down when substitute David Strelec went down in the area, and it was shaping up to be a frustrating first day in the dugout for Hellberg.

That narrative changed with 15 minutes remaining as Hackney sent in a corner from the right and Targett’s header sent it powering into the roof of the net to draw us back on level terms.

The momentum was firmly with Boro now and another corner produced what proved to be the winner in the 84 minute.

Hackney and Whittaker combined down the right to create a shooting opportunity for Whittaker, who sent it low into the bottom corner against his former club to send the home support into raptures.

It made it a perfect start to life on Teesside for Hellberg on a day full of drama.

Blistering Boro blew Hull City away with an incredible four-goal first half salvo at the MKM.

Kim Hellberg’s Reds were too hot to handle on Humberside, with the avalanche started by an excellent David Strelec finish on nine minutes.

Alex Gilbert – making his first appearance of the season – drilled in a second just after the half-hour and when Morgan Whittaker curled in soon after, Boro were well on the way to victory.

Riley McGree as good as made the points secure with a minute of the first half remaining and although the hosts pulled a goal back after the break, it was a tremendous away day for Boro.

Hellberg made three changes to the Boro XI which started the win over Derby County, with Gilbert brought in alongside McGree and Strelec. All three went on to play starring roles.

Our intentions were clear from the outset as we repeatedly won possession high up the field. The first occasion saw Gilbert nick the ball and Whittaker have a shot saved.

The opener came following a fine move down the left. Hayden Hackney sent McGree scampering down the wing and when his first-time cross was touched by Whittaker to Strelec, the Slovakian superbly caressed it into the roof of the net to more than justify his selection.

McGree and Tommy Conway both had sights of goal before Gilbert doubled Boro’s lead on 32 minutes.

Conway was the provider, winning the ball on the left and teeing up a shooting opportunity for Gilbert, who drilled it into the bottom corner from the edge of the area.

Whittaker got in on the act as Gilbert contributed again, finding his team-mate before watching as our No.11 tremendously curled in his fourth goal in as many games.

The first half scoring was completed shortly before the break. Again the left flank was a source of joy for the Reds as Alex Bangura raced away and picked out McGree, who controlled it before firing past a clutch of defenders and into the roof of the net.

Boro could not quite keep that momentum going at the start of the second half, and Hull pulled a goal back from the penalty spot just after the hour. Joe Gelhardt slotted home from the spot after Sol Brynn was adjudged to have tripped him in the box.

Hull were unable to produce a sustained period of pressure in their seach of a route back into the game, and Boro looked the likelier to score again the longer the half progressed.

Hackney and substitute Sam Silvera both had eye-catching attempts on goal as we aimed for a fifth.

It did not quite come, but that mattered little as Boro celebrated a brilliant three points.

Boro made it three wins out of three under Kim Hellberg with a controlled and clinical display at The Valley.

Riley McGree and Morgan Whittaker were again on target in the first half to reward the Teessiders’ general dominance.

Boro were composed after the break, but the hosts made it a nervy ending by pulling a goal back nine minutes before the end.

We saw it out, though, to seal another set of maximum points ahead of Saturday's home game against Queens Park Rangers.

There was one change to the Boro team which started Friday’s 4-1 win at Hull City, with Delano Burgzorg replacing the ill David Strelec in the line-up.

The early stages saw the Teessiders probe for an opening, and one almost came when Hayden Hackney’s left-foot drive was tipped wide by Thomas Kaminski.

Kaminski repeatedly thwarted Boro, saving well from Alex Bangura in our next attack.

We built up considerable pressure as the first half progressed. Callum Brittain’s cross was deflected narrowly past the post after hanging in the air, Alex Gilbert headed wide and Matt Targett fired into the side netting.

Tommy Conway went close with a fizzed effort which Kaminski brilliantly saved with his foot, but less than a minute later, we were in front.

Conway was at the heart of it, playing in Burgzorg down the right of the area. His excellent cutback found McGree and the Australian slammed home for his second goal in as many games.

We doubled our advantage on the counter in the final minute of first half stoppage time. Brittain and McGree combined to release Whittaker, who drove into the box and forced in a low effort at Kaminski’s near post to score for the fifth game in succession.

Boro would have expected a reaction from their hosts in the second half, and they got that as Charlton came out energetically.

The first chance after the break went to Boro, though, as Burgzorg raced through the centre and teed up McGree, whose low strike was kept out by Kaminski’s foot.

Kaminski also denied Conway at his near post as we continued to look the likelier team to add to the scoring.

Sol Brynn was forced into a superb save to deny substitute Ibrahim Fullah as Charlton aimed to build some late pressure.

Two substitutes almost combined to kill the game off for Boro, but Luke Ayling's header from Sverre Nypan's free-kick struck the crossbar.

Charlton pulled one back nine minutes from the end as George Edmundson headed into his own net.

That set up a potentially nervy close to the game, but Boro saw it out well to take the points.

Brilliant Boro made it four wins from four under Kim Hellberg with a dominant display against Queens Park Rangers.

The Teessiders were vibrant, fluid and clinical against a Queens Park Rangers side which went into the weekend inside the Sky Bet Championship’s play-off places.

After being frustrated in our search for an opener, David Strelec opened the scoring on the half-hour. Boro did not look back.

Morgan Whittaker continued his excellent form by doubling our lead shortly afterwards and Tommy Conway made it three from the spot early in the second half.

QPR pulled a goal back with a penalty of their own on 70 minutes, but Hellberg’s men saw it out to continue the Swede’s excellent start to life on Teesside as we strengthened our position in the top two.

Hellberg made three changes to the Boro team which started the 2-1 win at Charlton Athletic, with Luke Ayling, Strelec and Alan Browne replacing Alex Bangura, Delano Burgzorg and Alex Gilbert.

Boro were dominant in the first half but had to show patience to find a way through.

Conway almost opened the scoring inside two minutes after being played through by Whittaker. He beat Paul Nardi in a foot-race and knocked it over the Rangers goalkeeper, but Amadou Mbengue chased him towards the loose ball and just got there first.

Conway went closer still when he was again found by Whittaker, but after cutting onto his right foot, his strike was deflected inches past the post.

QPR sights of goal were rare but they got in behind through Rumarn Burrell on 19 minutes. His low cross was diverted out for a corner by Matt Targett.

The bulk of the attacking was being done by Boro, but a breakthrough was proving elusive.

Another counter saw Callum Brittain slide a superb ball across from the right. It found Strelec, but his first touch saw the ball squirm away and Nardi was able to close the angle and make a smothering save.

Riley McGree had two shots blocked and Rhys Norrington-Davies almost turned the ball into his own net, but Nardi made a sharp stop.

We were frustrated again before the half-hour when Conway tapped in from close range. The offside flag cut Boro’s celebrations short.

The Teessiders finally found a deserved breakthrough on 30 minutes. Hackney’s tremendous through ball played in Strelec and he made no mistake, finishing clinically for his third goal in Boro colours.

The lead was doubled in stunning fashion eight minutes before half-time. Sol Brynn claimed a high ball and arrowed a tremendous ball out to Whittaker on the right chancel. He glided forward, cut onto his left foot and picked out the bottom corner for his sixth goal in six games.

We kept our foot on the accelerator at the start of the second half and were awarded a penalty within four minutes of the restart after Koko Saito fouled Brittain in the area.

Conway stepped up to send Nardi the wrong way from the spot as he notched a deserved goal and took the acclaim of the Riverside.

Brynn was back in action on the hour, making a superb save at his near post from Mbengue.

He could do nothing to prevent QPR pulling one back 20 minutes from the end, though, with Nicolas Madsen slamming home from the spot.

Boro were quickly back on the front foot in pursuit of a fourth goal, with Kaly Sene and Hackney both having sights of goal.

Alan Browne made a vital interception at the other end to deny Paul Smyth a tap-in, and that was as close as Rangers got to halving the deficit as Boro saw it out.

Bristol City inflicted the first defeat of Kim Hellberg’s reign as our four-match winning run came to an end.

It was a frustrating afternoon for Boro as we dominated for large spells but were unable to convert the opportunities we created.

The hosts took the lead against the run of play inside the opening 20 minutes and after Boro had pushed strongly for an equaliser, the crucial second went the way of the Robins just after the hour.

The Teessiders again probed for a route back into the game, but it was not forthcoming as the home side saw it out for maximum points.

There was one change to the Boro team which started the 3-1 win over Queens Park Rangers, with Alex Gilbert replacing Alan Browne in midfield.

The Teessiders largely dominated the first half, but struggled to get efforts on target and were punished by a sucker punch at the other end.

Morgan Whittaker – searching for a seventh goal in as many games – struck the inside of the post inside the first four minutes after Tommy Conway had won the ball in the Bristol City area.

Callum Brittain’s dangerous ball across goal evaded a touch and it was a similar story when Hayden Hackney’s header dropped in the six-yard box but no one was there to apply the finishing touch.

Conway had a shot blocked on 17 minutes and the home side immediately countered to take the lead, with Emil Riis’ strike from the edge of the area going in.

Boro continued to have opportunities. We again regained possession inside the Robins’ penalty area and Conway played it back to Hackney, who was denied by a superb block.

Gilbert struck one narrowly wide via a deflection as we continued to search for an equaliser, but Bristol City could have gone further ahead on 45 minutes, with captain Jason Knight’s effort whistling over the bar.

Boro were back on the attack at the start of the second half and had an early sight of goal when Whittaker’s strike from the edge of the area was pushed wide by Max O’Leary.

It turned into a sustained period of pressure which saw Whittaker have another shot deflected wide before Gilbert’s sweet hit from distance was palmed away by O’Leary as the goalkeeper scrambled.

Boro were not quite able to make that period count, and Bristol City cashed in at the other end.

After Sol Brynn had brilliantly denied Sinclair Armstrong with a fingertip save, he was beaten from the resulting corner as substitute Rob Atkinson headed in.

That gave Boro a lot to do and although Hellberg's men threatened to make it a nervy ending for the home side, Bristol City did enough to record a clean sheet and with it, take maximum points.

Boro are back in action on Boxing Day when Blackburn Rovers visit the Riverside.

Boro were held to a Boxing Day goalless draw by a resolute Blackburn Rovers.

Kim Hellberg's men battled in vain for a breakthrough throughout an encounter which in truth could have gone either way.

A goal was not forthcoming at either end, but Boro remain second in the Sky Bet Championship heading into the final game of 2025.

Micah Hamilton was brought in for his first start of the season, replacing the injured Riley McGree in the XI.

He was part of a lively opening from Boro which yielded a number of openings and half-chances without the deadlock being broken.

Perhaps the best opportunity came nine minutes in when Callum Brittain fed Morgan Whittaker and he took a touch before seeing his prodded effort saved by Aynsley Pears.

Another sighter came when Whittaker – prominent throughout – played it to Tommy Conway and he had a shot blocked. The ball broke to Hayden Hackney, who was also denied by a sprawling defender.

Rovers looked dangerous when they went forward. Todd Cantwell thrashed into the side netting while vital interceptions from Luke Ayling, Brittain and George Edmundson snuffed out attacks.

A better opening for the visitors came after a fortunate ricochet. The ball was then helped through to Yuki Ohashi and he raced clear before pulling his shot wide.

Boro were back on top in the closing stages of the first half and were desperately unlucky not to take the lead in the 39th minute. Whittaker beat his man down the right of the area and unleashed a powerful strike which hit the inside of the post before somehow staying out.

Boro made two changes at half-time as Dael Fry replaced Edmundson – himself a first-half introduction – and Sverre Nypan came on for Hamilton.

Blackburn looked dangerous in the minutes which followed the break but Boro gradually took control.

Chances were difficult to come by as Rovers attempted to restrict us to efforts from distance, one of which saw Alex Gilbert clear the crossbar from 25 yards.

Boro were by no means dominant, with Blackburn possessing a continued threat, particularly on the break. Matty Litherland tested Sol Brynn following one of those counters.

Ayling excellently blocked from Moussa Baradji with 16 minutes remaining as Valerien Ismael's side fired another warning heading into the closing stages.

Hellberg's men looked to build some momentum in the final five minutes but Blackburn continued to restrict us. Brittain struck wide from 20 yards in a rare sight of goal.

That pattern continued until the end of proceedings as both teams took a point.

Boro suffered a frustrating end to 2025 as an early concession proved pivotal against Hull City.

The visitors took the lead on 12 minutes and proved difficult to break down as the Teessiders searched for a route back to parity.

Hull goalkeeper Ivor Pandur would not be beaten as we ended the calendar year with defeat, but still inside the Sky Bet Championship’s top two.

Alex Bangura, Alan Browne and Kaly Sene were brought into Boro’s starting XI in place of Alfie Jones, Micah Hamilton and David Strelec.

The game came less than a month on from Boro’s 4-1 win against the same opponents at the MKM, but this time it was Hull who struck the first blow.

Less than two minutes after Hayden Hackney had hit the post – though he had been flagged for offside – the Tigers went in front.

Kyle Joseph’s smart turn in the area produced an opening and after he was forced wide by Sol Brynn, the Hull man squared for Darko Gyabi to strike home.

Boro wrestled control of possession and probed for an equaliser, but chances were frustratingly difficult to come by in a tight first 45.

We were largely restricted to attempts from distance and blocked shots amid a sea of bodies as Hull maintained their lead into the half-time break, although there was a late opportunity for Tommy Conway, whose low shot was saved.

Boro looked increasingly threatening at the start of the second half as we began to put Hull under pressure.

Hackney was at the centre of much of our bright play. He had one strike from the edge of the box saved and saw another from distance drift wide, as did Alex Gilbert.

Boro began to test Pandur, who kept out a Bangura volley and a Delano Burgzorg effort, while he watched a Whittaker curler dip wide.

Pandur then had to be alert to deny Burgzorg again after the substitute turned in the area and struck goalwards, with the Hull goalkeeper pushing it over.

A succession of crosses resulted in unfortunate bounces and clearances as it began to look like it would be one of those nights for Boro.

Kim Hellberg's men continued to push for an equaliser until the death, but a breakthrough eluded them, with Burgzorg and Sontje Jansen both denied by blocks in stoppage time.

Boro will aim to kick-off 2026 in positive fashion, away to Derby County on New Year's Day.

Bobby Clark’s 70th-minute strike condemned Boro to a losing start to 2025.

It was an afternoon which saw the Teessiders made to pay for a number of missed opportunities, particularly in a dominant first half.

The contest was more even after the break and the crucial breakthrough went the way of the hosts as Clark danced his way into space before finishing well.

It was a breathless opening to the game from Boro, evoking memories of recent away trips to Hull City and Charlton Athletic.

No goals were forthcoming on this occasion, though, much to the away team’s frustration.

There were plenty of opportunities for Boro to go in front, the first of which fell to former Derby man Morgan Whittaker, who pulled wide from 20 yards after playing a give-and-go from a corner.

It looked like Hayden Hackney would put the Teessiders ahead when he combined with Delano Burgzorg and stared down Jacob Widell Zetterstrom, but the Rams goalkeeper did well to deny him.

Moments later, there was another chance as the superb Callum Brittain slid a ball through to Tommy Conway, but the striker could not quite get the ball from under his feet and was unable to get clean contact as it squirmed narrowly past the post.

Boro were denied a penalty on the quarter-hour when Matt Clarke challenged Burgzorg. Play continued and Whittaker saw his strike deflected just off target.

Openings were not as clear-cut in the remainder of the first half, although Conway had a volley sharply saved and Burgzorg pulled wide from 20 yards as Boro continued to dominate.

Derby’s sole effort on target in the first half came on 45 minutes as Joe Ward tried to catch out Sol Brynn with a free-kick, but the Boro goalkeeper was equal to it at his near post.

Burgzorg had two sights of goal in the first four minutes of the second half, testing Zetterstrom from 25 yards before firing low into the side netting from a similar position.

It looked like the hosts may break the deadlock when the ball was played in behind the Boro defence and Patrick Agyemang latched onto it. Brynn picked the perfect moment to pounce and close the angle before denying the striker a second goal in as many appearances against the Teessiders.

Boro responded well and worked some opportunities of their own. Whittaker hit one wide from the right of the area and Burgzorg shot over after a Matt Targett ball over the top.

It felt increasingly like the first goal would prove crucial, and it went the way of Derby on 70 minutes as Bobby Clark weaved himself into space before beating Brynn with a composed finish.

Boro mustered a strong response and there was almost an immediate leveller when Brittain was played in behind, but Zetterstrom saved well and the right-back was caught in the aftermath. The resulting injury forced his withdrawal.

The Teessiders kept pushing, but a goal remained elusive and Derby almost killed it off at the other end with a powerful Ben Brereton Diaz strike which Targett did brilliantly to block.

Time was by now running out as the game advanced through seven minutes of stoppage time. Derby saw it through to take maximum points.

Boro are back in action at home to Southampton on Sunday.

Morgan Whittaker scored his ninth and 10th goals of the season as Boro bounced back to winning ways on a buoyant afternoon at the Riverside.

The first game of 2026 on Teesside was marked in style as Kim Hellberg’s side brushed aside the challenge of a Southampton team aiming to make an immediate return to the Premier League.

There were no goals in an entertaining first half, although Adilson Malanda made a number of important interventions as he impressed on his Boro debut at the heart of the defence.

But the wait for goals was worth it after the break, with three arriving in a breathless 12-minute period.

Whittaker opened the scoring by finishing off a well-worked corner routine and Sam Silvera – brought back into the starting XI for the first time since Hellberg took charge – notched the second shortly afterwards.

It was three when Whittaker completed another fine move on 66 minutes, and there was no way back for a Saints side which had looked dangerous before the break.

Alan Browne finished the scoring in the final quarter-hour with his first goal in Boro colours to complete an excellent afternoon’s work.

A thoroughly watchable first half ended goalless, despite both teams working their way into fine attacking positions.

It was a spirited opening from Boro, who recovered from the blow of losing Alex Bangura to injury early on by putting the visitors under some pressure, despite being largely restricted to efforts from distance.

Luke Ayling saw a 25-yard strike deflected wide and Hayden Hackney curled narrowly past the post after a short free-kick routine.

Southampton boast some of the biggest attacking threats in the division, including Sky Bet Championship top scorer Adam Armstrong, who fired a volley not far wide on 13 minutes.

Former Boro man Finn Azaz also had a couple of sighters from distance, but the best chance of the first half fell to Saints midfielder Flynn Downes, whose 12-yard effort was excellently blocked by Malanda.

Boro worked their way into a number of promising positions throughout the half, particularly down the right, without being able to work a true shooting chance.

Some space did open up for Whittaker as half-time approached, and his sweet hit looked destined for the top corner before being deflected over.

The Teessiders had a let-off two minutes before the break when Tom Fellows was played in on goal before blazing over, with Southampton ending the first half on top.

Malanda had been hugely impressive in his first half of football as a Boro player, and that continued after half-time.

Armstrong looked certain to open the scoring in the 48th minute when the ball broke to him in the area, but Malanda prevented an outstanding block for the second time of the afternoon to keep the scores level.

Boro were looking enterprising going forward again, and the reward came after a short corner routine nine minutes into the second half.

Aidan Morris laid the ball back to Matt Targett 25 yards from goal and he split the defence with a tremendous through ball. Whittaker was on the end of it and finished first-time for his ninth goal of the season and a long-awaited Boro breakthrough.

One quickly became two at a pulsating Riverside when Ayling sent a terrific ball down the right and Silvera latched onto it before finishing low across Bazunu.

The confidence was flowing and a third arrived on 65 minutes, Morris’ low pass across the area finished by a delighted Whittaker as he hit double figures.

Hackney fired wide as Boro aimed to add further salt into the visitors’ wounds, as did Whittaker as he searched for his hat-trick.

The fourth goal came 14 minutes from time, Browne gratefully finishing from close range after Bazunu had parried Hackney’s strike.

There was a chance for Conway to add another in the closing stages, but his goalbound strike was blocked after he was played through by Whittaker.

Substitute Micah Hamilton also went close, shooting wide at the back post after good Boro play down the right.

The job had long since been done by the Teessiders, who can now look forward to Saturday's Emirates FA Cup trip to Fulham.

Boro fell just short of upsetting Premier League opponents Fulham in an entertaining FA Cup third round tie at Craven Cottage.

Kim Hellberg’s men were brilliant for long spells in the capital as they went after the Cottagers, who are ninth in the top division.

After twice threatening to open the scoring, the Teessiders went in front on the half-hour after carving Fulham open down the right, with Hayden Hackney on hand to provide the finishing touch from close range.

Luke Ayling made two vital blocks at the other end to keep Boro ahead going into the half-time break, but the introduction of in-form Harry Wilson in the second half proved vital for the hosts.

He curled them level less than three minutes after being brought on to change the momentum of the tie, with Emile Smith Rowe adding the winner for Fulham 13 minutes from time.

Boro battled for an equaliser as we looked to take the game to extra-time, but despite a continued valiant effort, fell just short, with Kevin adding Fulham's third in stoppage time.

Changes were minimal for Hellberg at Craven Cottage, with Alan Browne and Alex Gilbert starting in place of Alex Bangura and Delano Burgzorg.

The Boro made a bright start and went close to opening the scoring in the fourth minute. Morgan Whittaker worked the ball out to Sam Silvera down the right of the area and his centre found Tommy Conway, who was denied by the foot of Benjamin Lecomte.

Fulham’s Premier League quality was on show, but the home side were unable to seriously test Sol Brynn in the opening 45 minutes.

He comfortably caught a header from Jonah Kusi-Asare and kept out a tame Harrison Reed volley as the hosts looked to generate some pressure.

Boro were equal to it, though, and were looking the more dangerous of the two sides.

Gilbert sought out Hackney with a dinked cross to the back post, but the homegrown midfielder was just unable to provide the finishing touch.

Five minutes later, as the game approached the half-hour mark, he did.

A slick move by Boro involving Aidan Morris, Browne and Silvera saw Boro get in down the right of the area. Silvera brilliantly beat his man with a deft nutmeg and kept his composure to square for Hackney, who finished from close range as the away end erupted.

Far from content with a one-goal advantage, the Teessiders went in search of number two and Whittaker saw a 20-yard drive saved by Lecomte.

Fulham were at their most threatening in the closing stages of the half, and Boro were twice indebted to Ayling for remaining in front.

He stood tall to block from Cottagers forward Kevin before making an even better clearance, skipping back onto the line to hook away a goalbound strike from Jorge Cuenca.

Boro came out strongly at the start of the second half and it looked like the lead may be doubled in the 50th minute when Whittaker skipped past a defender, but his dangerous low ball across the area had no player waiting to convert it.

Fulham responded with a triple change, bringing on Raul Jimenez and Tom Cairney alongside Wilson.

Less than three minutes later, Wilson pulled the Cottagers back on level terms with a trademark finish, coming inside onto his left foot before curling into the bottom corner.

Many neutrals may have expected Boro to buckle at that stage, but Hellberg’s team reacted superbly, again attacking their hosts as they looked to regain their advantage.

Gilbert won the ball high up the pitch and fed it into Conway, who turned and thundered an effort against the top of the crossbar just moments before being brought off.

Boro were doing the bulk of the attacking and worked the ball into numerous dangerous areas, but they breathed a sigh of relief on 71 minutes when Kevin’s strike curled just past the post.

Brynn made an excellent double save, pushing away another Wilson curler before picking himself up well to deny Antonee Robinson on the rebound.

Fulham had now wrestled the momentum away from Boro and they made that count with 13 minutes remaining. Cairney split the defence with a fine pass and Smith Rowe’s clinical finish put the Cottagers ahead.

Again, the Teessiders’ response was impressive, and there was almost an immediate leveller. Whittaker was found inside the area and looked set to bring us level, but his strike went just past the post.

With Boro committing ever more men forward, Fulham struck a decisive third three minutes into stoppage time as Kevin finished Wilson's cross at the back post.

Boro won a dramatic three points on the road as Delano Burgzorg struck a terrific late winner at the Hawthorns.

Goals inside the final 15 minutes from Isaac Price and Jed Wallace pegged back Kim Hellberg’s men, who had been so impressive for much of the contest in earning a 2-0 lead.

After battling for a breakthrough against a Baggies team under new management, the Teessiders found it in the closing stages of the first half, with Alex Gilbert’s strike cannoning against the post and then defender Charlie Taylor on its way into the net.

Boro will have expected a strong second half response from West Brom in Eric Ramsay’s first game in charge, but what looked like a crucial second goal went to Hellberg’s side.

For the second league game in a row, Sam Silvera found the net with a superb low strike from the edge of the area 10 minutes after the break.

West Brom found a lifeline with a quarter-hour remaining as Isaac Price blasted in a free-kick from just outside the box.

They levelled on 80 minutes as substitute Jed Wallace picked out the bottom corner from the right of the area.

Both sides pushed for a winner but it was Boro who got the dramatic moment, Burgzorg firing home from Silvera's pass in the 90th minute.

Boro – unchanged from last week’s Emirates FA Cup defeat at Fulham – faced early West Brom pressure as a buoyed Hawthorns got behind Ramsay and his side.

Aune Heggebo stole possession high up the pitch inside the first three minutes but was unable to get a shot away, with Sol Brynn alert to the danger. The Boro goalkeeper closed the angle and spread himself well to deny the Norwegian.

Callum Styles’ dangerous corner caused Boro some jitters and the ball dropped to Chris Mepham, but his effort cleared the crossbar.

Boro survived the initial wave of positivity and began to exert control, dominating possession as the Baggies dropped further and further back.

Aidan Morris went close to opening the scoring, skipping inside from the left of the area before firing narrowly over.

The Teessiders’ task was to carve their hosts open, but West Brom did have one opening at the other end on the break. Brynn got down well to save from Karlan Grant.

Morgan Whittaker and Tommy Conway both saw low shots saved by Josh Griffiths in the Baggies goal as the pressure started to crank up.

The breakthrough then arrived three minutes before half-time. Hayden Hackney drifted in from the right and found Gilbert, whose sweet strike came back off the post before hitting Taylor and cannoning into the net.

Former Boro loanee Sam Iling-Junior fizzed one wide from the left of the area in what was close to the last action of the half as the away side took a one-goal advantage into the break.

A Baggies onslaught in response was not forthcoming immediately after half-time, although Heggebo did force a sharp save from Brynn when he turned and fired goalwards from 25 yards.

Boro again wrestled the initiative and, 10 minutes into the second period, the lead was doubled.

Hellberg’s men won the ball deep inside the West Brom half and Whittaker fed Silvera, who worked himself a shooting opportunity and drilled into the bottom corner from the edge of the area to continue his fine form.

Boro were looking dangerous with every attack, and almost found a third when Whittaker’s free-kick found Adilson Malanda and his header into the ground bounced just over.

West Brom began to push Boro back in search of a route back into the game as we entered the final 20 minutes.

Grant was denied by Brynn but, just minutes later, the hosts had a goal back when Price's powerful free-kick from just outside the box found the net.

Price curled narrowly wide with 12 minutes left but, moments later, the Baggies were level when the ball broke to the advancing Wallace and he made no mistake, carressing it into the bottom corner.

Brynn reacted brilliantly to spring from his line and deny Grant a clear strike at goal as it looked like West Brom may claim all three points.

The game was becoming increasingly stretched, and a winner looked possible at either end.
