An opening fell to Morris, who was denied by the body of Griffiths.

But it was Burgzorg who had the starring moment as the game hit the 90th minute, firing brilliantly into the bottom corner from Silvera's pass to seal a dramatic victory on the road.

Tommy Conway struck the winner as a superb second half fightback saw Boro make it three league wins from three.

We found ourselves a goal behind at half-time in the Potteries, with Tomas Rigo striking home from distance inside the first 15 minutes for Stoke City.

Kim Hellberg drew a strong response from his side after the break, with Alan Browne rattling in an equaliser within three minutes of the restart.

Conway – praised by his head coach in the lead-up to the game – fired in what proved to be the winner in the 59th minute after more excellent work from Browne.

Stoke were reduced to 10 men in the closing stages but responded to Conway's goal in spirited fashion.

They were unable to find a leveller, though, as Boro made it another set of maximum points on the road.

An unchanged Boro found it difficult to assert themselves in the first half as Stoke pressed well and forced mistakes.

It looked like the Potters may open Boro up down the left as early as the seventh minute, but Sorba Thomas’ dangerous low ball was excellently cut out by Adilson Malanda. Ben Wilmot headed wide from the resulting corner.

Stoke took the lead on the quarter-hour, with Rigo’s dipping strike from 25 yards squirming into the net.

Sol Brynn prevented a second as he tipped a Million Manhoef curler from outside the area onto the bar. That save came after a period of Boro possession which did not result in real opportunities for an equaliser.

Aidan Morris tested Stoke’s Tommy Simkin with a 20-yard effort which the goalkeeper spilled. Wilmot was fastest to the loose ball as he scrambled it to safety.

Simkin made a similar save from Matt Targett later in the half, and this time picked himself up well to also keep out Morgan Whittaker’s follow-up. The offside flag would have seen the rebound disallowed, however.

Boro were beginning to turn the tables on their hosts, but Stoke could have doubled their advantage with three minutes of the first half remaining. A ball over the top played in Lamine Cisse down the inside-right channel and Brynn did well to keep out his low shot with his foot.

Hellberg made two half-time changes, with Delano Burgzorg and Leo Castledine brought on in place of Sam Silvera and Alex Gilbert.

Boro’s attentions were made clear from the first whistle in the second half, with an increase in pace and intensity evident.

It bore dividends within three minutes of the restart. Castledine was involved in the build-up, beating his man before helping Boro work some space for Hayden Hackney in the inside-left channel. His powerful low strike was parried by Simkin, who then made a similar stop from Morris. The ball squirmed away and hit Whittaker before rolling towards Browne, who rifled it into the roof of the net to bring us back on level terms.

The Teessiders were immediately on the attack again after kick-off, with Hackney having a shot deflected wide and Browne flicking past the post from a Whittaker cross.

Boro needed to remain alert at the other end, and were warned on 54 minutes when Manhoef struck over from 20 yards.

But it was mainly the away team making the most impact going forward, and the quick turnaround was completed just before the hour.

Browne turned provider this time, getting in down the right before producing a tremendous low cross to the back post. It found Conway, who adjusted his body well and turned in from close range in front of a jubilant away support.

Conway almost had a quickfire double, but his powerful drive from 20 yards was kept out by the strong right hand of Simkin.

Stoke’s task was made tougher with 13 minutes remaining when Bosun Lawal received his second yellow card, leaving his team with 10 men for the closing stages.

They remained dangerous, though, with Brynn forced to claw away set pieces on multiple occasions to prevent chances on goal.

Burgzorg could have sealed it towards the end, but his blasted effort flew wide.

It mattered not, though, as Boro saw out the closing stages to seal another vital win.

Tommy Conway was at the double as Boro made it four league wins from four with a scintillating performance at the Riverside.

A fast start by Boro was rewarded with a goal inside the first nine minutes as Alan Browne struck against his former club.

Matt Targett lifted a delicious ball over from the left and Browne got on the end of it after timing his run to perfection. He took a touch to steady himself before slotting home left-footed for his third goal in four league games.

Kim Hellberg’s men went two in front before the half-hour as Conway dispatched his second goal in as many matches, finishing well after latching onto a tremendous ball from Luke Ayling.

Morgan Whittaker made it three as the game approached half-time, pouncing on a loose ball in the area before firing in from 12 yards after another period of strong Boro pressure.

Preston’s task was made harder less than five minutes into the second half as Jordan Storey was sent off for pulling down Conway, and it was four soon after as Conway turned home the rebound from a Leo Castledine free-kick.

There were no further goals, but Boro dominated the remainder of the proceedings to record a comfortable win.

Boro went into the game looking to lay down a marker in one of two lunchtime kick-offs in the Sky Bet Championship.

Castledine was handed a first start and captain Dael Fry returned to the XI, but it was Preston who had the first sights of goal.

A short corner inside the first minute led to a strike from Alfie Devine which Fry blocked, and another corner saw the ball drop to Daniel Jebbison, who forced Sol Brynn to save with his feet.

Boro quickly got a grip of proceedings before breaking the deadlock on nine minutes through the combination of Targett’s ball and Browne’s cool finish.

Browne could have had a second in the 23rd minute. Ayling sent in an inch-perfect pass from the right and the Irishman made space for himself by deftly rolling the ball past his defender, but this time his left-foot shot went wide.

Ayling was the provider again as Boro doubled their lead. This time he picked out Conway with a sumptuous through ball from his own half and the forward powered his way through before firing low and hard. Goalkeeper Jack Walton got a touch to it, but the ball arrowed into the bottom corner as the Riverside erupted.

The Teessiders had a stranglehold on the match and built up another head of steam towards half-time.

Aidan Morris saw a sweet strike from distance deflected wide, Ayling’s audacious flick was saved and Castledine forced Walton into a smart low save.

The third goal arrived three minutes before half-time. A Boro corner was claimed by Walton and the goalkeeper rolled the ball out to Lewis Gibson inside his own penalty area. Whittaker spotted the opportunity, pouncing on the Preston defender before stealing possession and finishing clinically for his 11th of the season.

Boro were on the front foot again from the start of the second half and there was a quick half-chance for Castledine, who received the ball with his back to goal, turned and drilled wide from 20 yards.

Storey was dismissed after Conway pounced on a loose touch and began to arrow towards goal, before the Preston defender pulled him down to deny a goalscoring opportunity.

It did not take long for Boro to take full advantage. After a free-kick was awarded 20 yards from goal, Castledine’s whipped effort was parried by Walton and Conway snaffled up the opportunity for his second.

Conway was withdrawn as part of a triple change shortly afterwards, but the chances kept coming for Boro.

Hayden Hackney fired over from the edge of the area after some space opened up for him and substitute Alex Gilbert saw a drive from distance turned around the post by Walton.

There were to be no further goals, despite continued Boro dominance, but no one inside the Riverside was complaining.

We are back at home next Saturday, aiming to make it five league wins on the bounce against Norwich City.

Hayden Hackney’s first half stunner delivered Boro a hard-fought and merited fifth Sky Bet Championship win in a row.

Hackney’s 25-yard piledriver was the difference against an in-form Norwich City side which gave the Teessiders a true test of their credentials.

Boro’s breakthrough came on 17 minutes as a result of a successful high press, with Hackney adding the gloss with a rising drive into the top corner.

The goal came after a small period of Norwich pressure but Kim Hellberg’s side were the better team from there, demonstrating their quality and confidence before seeing the game out with determination and grit.

The result extended Boro’s winning run to five league games ahead of next Monday’s trip to Sheffield United.

Callum Brittain and Riley McGree were brought into the Boro starting XI, having been on the bench for last week’s 4-0 win over Preston North End.

Boro enjoyed a bright opening, with Hackney having an effort from range pushed away by Vladan Kovacevic before Morgan Whittaker was denied by a close-range block.

Norwich arrived at the Riverside on a four-match winning streak of their own, and began to demonstrate why.

The dangerous Jovon Makama saw a 25-yard strike beaten away by Sol Brynn. The Boro goalkeeper later made a better save but Norwich kept the ball alive, with Brynn forced into another sharp stop from Ali Ahmed.

Boro’s high press had threatened to force Norwich into a mistake throughout the early stages, and the forward line got its reward on 17 minutes.

Tommy Conway stole possession deep inside the Norwich half and when Riley McGree laid it off to Hackney, the midfielder stole the show. His unstoppable, rising 25-yard drive arrowed its way into the top corner to open the scoring and puncture the momentum Norwich had been looking to build.

Boro’s confidence shone through in a number of fine moves and patterns of play as Hellberg’s men went in search of a second.

Norwich managed to stem the tide, though, and went close to an equaliser when Ahmed’s back header from a free-kick dropped narrowly wide of Brynn’s left-hand post.

Boro were relatively comfortable with their one-goal advantage, but chances for a second were at a premium.

Aidan Morris tested Kovacevic after an eye-catching piece of play from the Teessiders and Whittaker was denied by a block after some fine work in the middle by McGree.

Boro took the one-goal advantage into the interval, and it was well-earned.

We started the second half like a team on a mission and almost opened Norwich up within 60 seconds of the restart, with Conway’s dangerous low ball narrowly evading a touch.

Some excellent interplay led to a ball by Adilson Malanda which Whittaker fired wide, before some major controversy on 55 minutes.

Luke Ayling picked out Conway with a tremendous ball over the top and the Boro striker took it around Kovacevic before being cleaned out by the goalkeeper, five yards outside the Norwich penalty area. A yellow card was the Bosnian’s punishment before he saved the resulting free-kick from Matt Targett.

Norwich attempted to exert some pressure on Boro the longer the second half went on, and the longer the game remained at 1-0, the more the home support roared their team on.

There was a scare on 78 minutes when a Makama half-volley whistled over the crossbar, but Boro were defending valiantly when required.

Conway had delivered a tireless performance and he found the energy to attack from the left and fire a low shot which Kovacevic got down to save.

Makama looked like he might rescue a point for Norwich with a minute to go, but Dael Fry raced back after Makama touched the ball round Brynn and made an outstanding tackle to prevent a certain goal.

That proved to be the last major chance for the visitors as Boro saw it out for a huge three points.

Electric Boro made it six league wins from six with an outstanding performance at Bramall Lane.

After withstanding some early pressure from the Blades, Kim Hellberg’s men began to turn the screw, creating a number of openings.

The breakthrough came in the 19th minute when some excellent interplay saw Riley McGree feed the ball through to Tommy Conway, who struck home his fourth goal in four games.

McGree was at the heart of so many of Boro’s brightest work, and after Sol Brynn had produced an outstanding save at the other end, the Australian doubled the Teessiders’ lead.

It came a minute before the break after Hayden Hackney’s dipping drive had come back off the post. McGree was alert to it and did brilliantly to guide a controlled header into an empty net and send the away end into raptures.

Boro largely controlled the second half but the home side came back strongly, with Patrick Bamford halving the deficit with 16 minutes remaining.

Hellberg's side were resolute in what was a difficult ending to the game - home midfielder Joe Rothwell was sent off in the closing stages - sealing a vital three points and climbing to the top of the table.

Kicking off after the rest of the Sky Bet Championship’s Friday, Saturday and Sunday outings, it was always likely to be a keenly-fought contest.

The Blades were unbeaten in their previous eight league home matches – winning six of them – and started well against and unchanged Boro team.

Gus Hamer – last year’s Championship Player of the Season – tested Brynn early with a 10-yard curler, and after the hosts kept the ball alive, Sydie Peck sliced over a loose ball on the edge of the area.

It was an all-action start to the game at both ends, and Boro’s first opening came when Hackney fed it through to Conway and he fired over when well-placed down the left of the area.

There were strikes from distance by Ollie Arblaster and Peck for the Blades, but Boro fired a warning to their hosts with a well-worked corner routine which led to a cross from Luke Ayling which Adilson Malanda headed goalwards, only to be denied by home goalkeeper Michael Cooper.

There was barely time to catch breath. Malanda blocked well from Andre Brooks, and at the other end, Cooper saved from Whittaker, who was a constant threat. He fired another opportunity wide minutes later.

It had felt for some time that a goal was in the offing, and it came on 19 minutes.

Ayling worked the ball through to Whittaker, who received it with his back to goal and laid it off to McGree. He weighted his through ball to Conway perfectly, and the in-form forward latched onto it, taking a couple of touches to get it out of his feet before stroking into the bottom corner.

There were chances to make it two. A swift counter-attack saw Callum Brittain’s low cross flicked wide by Conway, and Hackney arrowed one into the side netting from outside the area.

Many Blades fans thought their side had equalised on the half-hour when a ball over from the left found former Boro man Bamford. He chested it down and his powerful half-volley rippled the net, but unfortunately for the hosts, it was the wrong side of the post.

Hamer was next to go close, with his sweet low strike from 12 yards brilliantly tipped wide by Brynn, who showed razor-sharp reactions.

Conway and Whittaker both went close, denied by a block and a low Cooper save respectively, but there was still time for Boro to go two ahead before half-time.

Hackney dribbled forward and sent a dipping drive against the upright from 20 yards. The ball squirmed back out and fastest to it was McGree, who grabbed himself a deserved goal with a cool header into an empty net from close range.

Boro started the second half well but Sheffield United had the first sight of goal. Callum O’Hare’s low ball across the face of goal begged a touch, but none was forthcoming.

We started to exert some pressure again after that, but Cooper was largely untested.

Whittaker fired over from the edge of the box after Conway had failed to get clean contact on his effort.

Substitute Alex Gilbert fed a ball through to Hackney and a block denied him with 20 minutes remaining, before the Blades began to get on top.

They halved the deficit on 74 minutes, with Hamer threading it to Bamford, who made no mistake with a clinical finish.

Brynn made an outstanding save with his foot to deny substitute Tyrese Campbell less than a minute later as the Blades almost made it a quickfire double.

The home side's task was made more difficult in the 80th minute when midfielder Rothwell was shown a straight red card for a poor challenge on Alan Browne.

They continued to push for an equaliser, but Boro held firm for a crucial set of maximum points.

Boro’s six-match winning run came to an end as a clinical Coventry City side ran out 3-1 winners.

In a high-stakes top-of-the-table clash, Haji Wright scored a hat-trick to deliver maximum points for the Sky Blues.

The American’s low finish gave Frank Lampard’s side the lead on 21 minutes, and he doubled their advantage 10 minutes into a second half which Boro had started well.

Riley McGree blasted Kim Hellberg’s men back into it with a tremendous finish, but within minutes, Coventry were two in front again as Wright dispatched a penalty.

The third Coventry goal proved crucial as Boro searched in vain for another route back into the game.

Boro were unbeaten from the excellent 2-1 win at Sheffield United the previous Monday, but Coventry came out with impressive intensity from the first whistle to put their visitors on the back foot.

There was almost a goal inside the first two minutes. Tatsuhiro Sakamoto teased in a superb delivery from the right and Haji Wright headed it against the post.

Boro responded well and Morgan Whittaker whistled over from distance, but Coventry’s press was causing the Teessiders problems at the other end.

After winning the ball high in the seventh minute, Jack Rudoni forced Adilson Malanda into a brave block.

The Sky Blues broke the deadlock just before the midway point in the first half. Jack Rudoni received the ball inside the area and played it across to Wright, whose low prod found the net.

Ephron Mason-Clark drifted inside from the left and dragged a shot narrowly wide as the home side looked to press home their advantage, and it took until the period immediately before half-time for Boro to begin to serious threaten.

Whittaker almost equalised with five minutes left of the half. Matt Targett picked him out with a terrific ball from the left and the forward’s header was goalbound before being blocked.

Luke Ayling was also denied by a block from the resulting corner, while at the other end, a long ball from Carl Rushworth found Mason-Clark, who controlled well and forced Sol Brynn into a low save.

Boro started the second half brightly and had an early opportunity, with Whittaker heading narrowly over from a McGree cross.

The Teessiders were pressing their opponents back and after some intricate play from the left, Hayden Hackney drew a smart stop from Rushworth.

The save drew immediate further dividends for the hosts. Rushworth launched the ball straight down the field and found Wright, who ruthlessly finished with his left foot to puncture Boro’s recent momentum.

The striker had a sight of a hat-trick on 64 minutes, but slammed wide from the edge of the box.

Almost immediately, Boro were agonisingly close to pulling a goal back. Out of nowhere, substitute Jeremy Sarmiento curled a tremendous strike from the left of the area which hit the inside of the post and somehow stayed out.

McGree did get the Teessiders back to within one of the Sky Blues midway through the second half. Callum Brittain’s dangerous ball found Aidan Morris and his shot deflected into the path of McGree, who rifled it into the roof of the net.

Boro were the team with the wind in their sails, but it was taken out of them moments later. Targett was punished for a handball in the area and Wright made no mistake from the spot, picking out the bottom corner.

The away side found themselves back in the position of searching for two goals, and the game became stretched as a result.

David Strelec had a sighter with 12 minutes left, but Rushworth was equal to his strike. The goalkeeper also denied McGree as the game entered its final five minutes, and Morris had a goalbound effort blocked in the closing stages.

Despite much probing, there was to be no late lifeline for Boro, who will aim to bounce back in Saturday's home game against Oxford United.

Boro were unable to break down a dogged Oxford United side in a frustrating afternoon at the Riverside.

In a match of importance at both ends of the Sky Bet Championship table, Kim Hellberg’s men pushed and pushed for a breakthrough against the relegation battlers.

However, it was not forthcoming as the U’s – who hit the woodwork twice in the first half – took a share of the spoils.

Boro’s dominance of possession started early, but Oxford had an effort at goal inside the first minute, with Myles Peart-Harris blazing over from distance.

The U’s looked dangerous on the break. Jeon Jin-Woo had two efforts from outside the area, one of which was comfortably gathered by Sol Brynn while the other was blocked by the charging Tommy Conway.

Jeremy Sarmiento – one of three players introduced to the starting line-up – had a half-chance on 18 minutes, but was off-balance as he connected with Callum Brittain’s cross and sent the ball over.

The closest either side came in the first half was a stunning strike from long-range by Stanley Mills which crashed against the crossbar.

But Boro were largely camped in Oxford’s half, and began pushing their opponents back further as the game approached half-time.

David Strelec and Matt Targett both tested U’s goalkeeper Jamie Cumming from the edge of the area, and Aidan Morris bent one wide from distance.

The Teessiders were almost hit by a sucker-punch on the stroke of the break when Jack Currie’s cross was helped on by Mills to Peart-Harris, who prodded against the base of the post.

Boro’s territorial advantage was even more marked after half-time, and there was an opening within 25 seconds of the restart, with Sarmiento forcing a save from Cumming.

Hayden Hackney fired a volley over, Conway had a drive held by Cumming, Morgan Whittaker curled wide from outside the area and Hackney sent a free-kick over, all inside the first 20 minutes of the half.

Whittaker saw another shot saved by Cumming before the Oxford goalkeeper made his best stop yet, brilliantly denying Conway with his foot after Strelec’s through ball had split the defence.

There was a moment of danger at the other end when Will Vaulks’ long throw caused problems and was pushed over by Brynn, but that was a rare foray into the final third by Oxford.

The breakthrough almost came for Boro on 78 minutes. Brittain chipped the ball forward, Whittaker nodded it on and U’s defender Christ Makosso headed it narrowly past his own post.

There was another agonising moment soon after when Hackney picked out Brittain and he bore down on goal, only to be denied by a last-ditch block.

Boro continued to commit bodies forward in search of a dramatic winner, but Oxford could not be broken down.

The Teessiders will aim to return to winning ways on Tuesday, at home to Leicester City.

Riley McGree’s equaliser sealed a point for Boro against Leicester City at the Riverside.

The in-form Australian pulled us level two minutes into first half stoppage time, cancelling out an early header from Leicester’s Caleb Okoli.

It was another night which saw Kim Hellberg’s men enjoy the bulk of the possession and territory, but opportunities proved difficult to come by until the closing stages as the Foxes took a share of the spoils.

Hellberg made three changes to the team which started Saturday’s draw with Oxford United, re-introducing Luke Ayling, Alan Browne and McGree to the XI.

The first strike at goal came inside the first two minutes, with Leicester goalkeeper Asmir Begovic punching away a Matt Targett free-kick.

Boro’s press was effective in the early stages as the Foxes were regularly forced backwards, but the visitors’ threat on the counter was evident.

Gary Rowett’s team took the lead against the run of play on 18 minutes, with Divine Mukasa’s teasing free-kick from the right headed in by Okoli.

Sol Brynn gathered a powerful strike from distance by Bobby De Cordova-Reid shortly afterwards before Boro began to create opportunities of their own, working their way into several dangerous positions.

Tommy Conway was at the centre of much of our bright play. On one occasion, he got in behind on the left and pulled a ball across which begged a finish, but no team-mate was there to convert.

The Scotland international was a whisker away from pulling the Teessiders level 10 minutes before half-time, whistling a strike narrowly wide via a deflection, while Hayden Hackney later slammed into the side netting.

Our equaliser came two minutes into four added at the end of the first half, and it was an excellently-worked goal. McGree combined with Hackney and he played in Conway down the left of the area. He pulled it across goal, where the onrushing McGree was on hand to stroke past Begovic.

Boro went into half-time with the momentum, but chances were difficult to come by after the break.

In fact, it was Leicester who almost scored the game’s third goal two minutes after the restart. Luke Thomas lifted a ball over the top and after Boro were unable to get it clear, Patson Daka guided a header narrowly past the upright.

Boro continued to have the bulk of the possession, without seriously threatening to go in front.

There was another close shave at the other end when Abdul Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right dropped just the wrong side of the post.

Boro’s first real chance of the second half came with 17 minutes remaining. Callum Brittain was found high on the right and his low cross was met by substitute David Strelec, who prodded wide.

McGree fired off target from the edge of the area soon after as he continued to pose a huge threat to the visitors.

He went close to an equaliser with six minutes left, forcing his way through the middle before seeing a deflected strike saved by the legs of Begovic. Boro kept the ball alive and a huge penalty appeal for handball was waved away.

Boro battled to the final whistle in search of a dramatic late winner, but Leicester held firm to boost their survival hopes.

Matt Targett enjoyed a dream return to the second city as his first half double helped to inflict a rare home defeat on Birmingham City.

Tasked with more attacking responsibilities after being deployed at left wing-back, the former Aston Villa man struck on 13 and 26 minutes to put the home side on the back foot.

It was a double which set Boro on the way to inflicting just a second St Andrew’s league defeat of the season on Birmingham, who had lost just one of their previous 41 league games on home soil.

There was a strong second half response from the Blues, who pulled a goal back early with a finish from Marvin Ducksch.

But Boro were not to be denied, restoring the two-goal advantage on the hour mark thanks to a tremendous header from David Strelec.

That goal proved pivotal as Kim Hellberg’s men returned to winning ways in excellent fashion, following a run of two draws and a defeat.

Hellberg opted to switch formations in the second city, with Targett and Callum Brittain operating as full-backs as part of a five-man defence.

The change saw Dael Fry and Strelec brought into the starting XI, but play-off chasing Birmingham started well in a bouncing atmosphere.

Sol Brynn was called into action in just the third minute, springing to his left to push a powerful drive from Tommy Doyle around the post.

Brittain blocked well from Demarai Gray in the early stages, too, with Boro putting bodies on the line to thwart their hosts’ promising start.

There had been a couple of warning signs for Birmingham as the Teessiders came close to forcing a way through, finding joy between the lines and almost springing the offside trap.

That is how the crucial opening goal was conjured on 13 minutes.

Aidan Morris clipped a superb ball over the top and Targett was quickest to it, chesting it down before making use of several yards of space to stroke past James Beadle in the Birmingham goal.

Targett was a key attacking threat down the left, but also from set-pieces.

His free-kick in the 22nd minute was only headed as far as Morris, who sent a volley over as he sought his first goal in Boro colours.

Boro scored a second soon after, and again it was Targett who struck the decisive blow.

Tommy Conway stole possession just outside the Birmingham box and Hayden Hackney helped it forward, the ball ricocheted back to the Boro No.7. He responded with superb composure as he controlled the ball before weighting a perfect pass to Targett, who was able to slide in his second.

Birmingham attempted to reduce the arrears in the closing stages of the first half, but the closest they came to troubling Brynn was a Christoph Klarer header which the goalkeeper comfortably saved at his near post.

Boro will have expected a strong Blues response at the start of the second half, and that is what they got.

Within three minutes of the restart, the home side had a goal back as Jay Stansfield peeled away down the right of the area and pulled the ball back for Ducksch, who finished well from the edge of the box.

Now with the momentum, Birmingham went in search of an equaliser and could have got it when Ducksch took aim from the edge of the box, but Brynn pushed his effort around the post.

Boro took the sting out of the Blues fightback and began to threaten again at the other end, with Adilson Malanda seeing a half-volley deflected wide.

The resulting corner saw the game’s vital fourth goal go the way of the men from Teesside. Although the initial delivery was half-cleared, Boro kept the ball alive and Luke Ayling curled in a tremendous cross from the left. It found the towering Strelec, and the Slovakian striker executed his header perfectly, sending it arrowing into the net via the inside of the post to send the travelling support into raptures.

It proved to be Strelec’s final contribution as he was immediately replaced by Morgan Whittaker, but it was far from the end of Boro’s pushing forward.

Conway forced a mistake from Beadle, charging the goalkeeper down, only for the ball to ricochet against the Scotland international and into the goalkeeper’s hands.

Boro controlled the game from there, seeing it out for a superb three points.

Boro made it two away wins from two with a dominant performance at Loftus Road.

It was a super Sunday in the capital for Kim Hellberg’s men, who made their authority in possession count.

The crucial breakthrough came on 20 minutes, with Morgan Whittaker’s strike bundled in by David Strelec on the goal-line as the Slovakian celebrated his second goal in as many games.

Boro’s territorial advantage continued in the second half, and that was rewarded on 68 minutes as Alan Browne headed in our second.

Hayden Hackney added a superb third less than four minutes later, and Tommy Conway scored a fourth from the spot to seal the points and cap off an excellent display on the road.

Hellberg made two changes to the Boro team which started the 3-1 win at Birmingham City last Monday, with Browne and Whittaker replacing Adilson Malanda and Tommy Conway.

The Teessiders were quickly into their stride, stroking the ball about with confidence and bravery to pen their hosts deep inside their own half.

Sol Brynn was called into early action, but his low save from a Richard Kone drive was comfortable.

The first 20 minutes were largely without goalscoring opportunities, but Boro were dominant in possession and by the time the deadlock was broken, it was beginning to feel inevitable.

It came thanks to some fine play down the left. Hackney found the elusive Riley McGree in space and his superb pass across the area presented Whittaker with a golden chance. His first stabbed effort was blocked but the ball ricocheted back to him and his second strike hit Strelec on the line before trickling its way in.

QPR’s response saw Harvey Vale having an off-target strike blocked by Dael Fry and Isaac Hayden seeing a header palmed away by Brynn.

But it was Boro who looked the likelier to score the second, and it almost came just beyond the half-hour when Hackney bent the ball inches past the post.

In first half stoppage time, Luke Ayling flicked wide from a Callum Brittain corner, with Boro forced to settle for a one-goal advantage from their 71% possession.

Rangers attempted a fightback in the early stages of the second half and forced two corners, but the first attempt after the interval was Boro’s, with Browne unable to get clean contact on a McGree cross.

Aidan Morris – who produced a tremendous display in midfield – then caused problems for the home side with a driving run through the centre before finding Strelec, whose strike was saved by Joe Walsh.

QPR went up the other end and Hayden was found in space, only for Ayling to excellently block his effort.

The game was beginning to become stretched, with attempts at goal at both ends, but Boro regained control and then made it count.

Matt Targett sent a volley wide before, midway through the second half, the vital second goal came.

Ayling’s audacious effort came back off the crossbar and first to react was Browne as he ruthlessly headed into the roof of the net.

McGree had a strike saved by Walsh less than four minutes later but that only delayed Boro’s third goal by moments, and it came in some style.

Substitute Conway fed the ball inside from the left and after McGree dummied, Hackney did the rest. His superb, curling strike from the left of the area bent its way into the far corner via a kiss of the post to send the sold-out away end into raptures.

Vale struck the post for the hosts with a sweet strike from outside the area, but the final goal was at the other end, where Conway won and duly dispatched a penalty to put a bow on the three points for the Teessiders.

Boro were denied a third straight victory as Charlton Athletic took the points from the Riverside.

Conor Coady’s goal 14 minutes into the second half proved pivotal for the visitors as the Teessiders dominated possession and created numerous chances, only to fail to find the net.

It was a night of frustration for Kim Hellberg’s side, who will bid to bounce back at home to Bristol City on Saturday.

Boro started well and almost immediately dominated possession, pushing their opponents deep inside their own half.

Inside the first three minutes, Hayden Hackney received the ball just inside the six-yard box before being crowded out and Morgan Whittaker flashed a dangerous ball across the face of goal which no one could get on the end of.

David Strelec thumped over from the edge of the area, Matt Targett sliced a good chance wide and Strelec was denied by a Keenan Gough block as Boro pumped up the pressure.

Callum Brittain was among the others to have a sight of goal, with his left-foot drive saved low by Will Mannion.

Charlton had a decent spell midway through the first half. Adilson Malanda was forced to make a superb block from Charlie Kelman, who also drew a sharp save from Sol Brynn.

But it was Boro who were by far the more threatening team, and just beyond the half-hour, the breakthrough almost came.

A ball was slid into the area from the left and after Targett appeared to be bundled over – with no penalty given – it broke to Aidan Morris, who was denied a first Boro goal by the fingertips of Mannion and then the crossbar.

Whittaker saw a 20-yard strike scooped wide by Mannion and Targett had a header blocked as the hosts continued to be frustrated into the half-time break.

The second half started in the same vain, with Malanda’s stabbed effort from a Brittain free-kick deflected wide.

But against the run of play, the visitors took the lead just before the hour as Coady hooked in from a Harry Clarke long throw.

Boro’s response was instant, and there was almost an equaliser as Morris’ strike was blocked by Coady before a big penalty appeal was waved away.

The home side locked Charlton deep inside their own territory in search of a leveller, and there was a chance for one when Morris’ cross found substitute Leo Castledine, who headed over.

Conway sliced over and Hackney had a strike deflected over as the game entered its final 15 minutes, and it looked set to be a night of disappointment for Hellberg’s men.

Castledine also had a drive from 20 yards saved and Morris had a goalbound effort blocked with less than three minutes remaining.

There was also a late chance for Hackney, whose shot from inside the area nestled in the arms of Mannion, and Malanda, whose hooked effort was also saved.

Boro kept pushing and pushing for an equaliser through what were five minutes of stoppage time - Castledine headed the clearest opportunity wide - but Charlton would not be broken down as they took the points.

Boro were denied a return to winning ways by a 96th-minute equaliser.

A thumping finish from Leo Castledine on 65 minutes looked set to hand Kim Hellberg's men a deserved three points.

But Adam Randell headed in an equaliser deep into stoppage time as Bristol City claimed a point.

Boro started the game brightly and had an early chance when Hayden Hackney’s cross was met by Tommy Conway, but his back-post header cleared the crossbar.

Callum Brittain had a shot blocked and Adilson Malanda was just unable to get clean contact on an inviting Aidan Morris cross as the Teessiders were unable to make the early pressure count.

Boro were dominant in possession as Bristol City were content to sit deep, but it was almost a set-piece which broke the deadlock seven minutes before half-time.

Matt Targett curled in a corner from the right and after it beat two defenders, it looked set to find its way in at the near post before Robins goalkeeper Radek Vitek made a last-ditch save with his foot.

There was another chance in stoppage time when a corner was half-cleared to Riley McGree, whose firm strike was held by Vitek.

The visitors’ first attempt came seven minutes into the second half, with Emil Riis’ effort from the edge of the area drifting wide.

It was then that Boro cranked things up, with Brittain firing the first warning with a sweet hit which deflected wide.

We worked the resulting corner short and Morris collected the ball just outside box. His shot was spilled by Vitek, who then did brilliantly to keep out Alan Browne’s follow-up with his feet and then sprung onto his line to prevent the ball from crossing it.

There was another opening on the hour when Targett’s cross found Browne and his header was saved by Vitek.

The breakthrough finally came on 65 minutes, and it was an excellently-worked goal by Boro. Hackney was found in space down the right and he weighted a perfect low ball into the centre, where substitute Castledine was on hand to crash in his first goal in Boro colours, via the underside of the bar.

Boro lost Hackney to injury soon after but the dominance on the ball continued, with Morris testing Vitek with another strike from outside the area.

Another substitute, David Strelec, could have settled things with nine minutes left, but Vitek saved the one-on-one chance with his foot.

Luke Ayling also went close with a flicked header which went just past the post, before Brittain came to the rescue at the other end with a superbly timed tackle on Max Bird.

There was a scare for Boro when Cameron Pring flicked a header narrowly wide from a free-kick.

And then, in the six of seven added minutes, Adam Randell thumped in a header from a corner as the visitors took a point.

Boro were frustrated by a resolute Blackburn Rovers side at Ewood Park.

Kim Hellberg’s side – looking for a return to winning ways – dominated possession and territory, and created a number of chances to break the deadlock, particularly in the first half.

Blackburn held firm, though, to take a share of the spoils as they boosted their survival bid.

Boro looked by far the likelier team to score in a first half which proved to be frustrating in front of goal.

A succession of corners were cleared by the hosts but one of them only went as far as Luke Ayling, who drew a smart low stop from Rovers goalkeeper Balazs Toth.

A better chance fell to Aidan Morris after the Teessiders worked the ball through to him in the inside-right channel, but the American’s powerful strike whistled into the side netting.

Boro kept attempting to work their way through and another opening came after some fine work through the centre by Riley McGree. He then teed up Alan Browne, who dragged the ball onto his left foot and then saw his effort blocked.

Blackburn’s sole attempt at goal in the first half came on 34 minutes, with Sol Brynn keeping out Ryoya Morishita’s low drive.

The closest Boro came to breaking the deadlock arguably came just before half-time. Tommy Conway broke away down the left, beat a defender and sent an excellent ball across the area for David Strelec, whose well-hit strike was excellently tipped over by Toth.

Roared on by a sold-out away end of almost 7,400 Boro fans, the Teessiders’ dominance on the ball was even more pronounced after the interval.

Opportunities were harder to come by, though, as the home side dropped deeper. One fell to Morris after some excellent work from Conway, but his shot lacked the power to seriously trouble Toth.

Boro worked their way into a series of promising attacking areas, but were unable to find the quality required to break the deadlock.

The closest they came in the second half followed a low ball into the area by Leo Castledine which eventually found its way to Browne, only for a block to deny him.

The Teessiders will now need to wait until after the international break to attempt to return to winning ways.

Boro suffered a Good Friday defeat as Millwall came from behind to win at the Riverside.

A dominant first half display produced one goal for Kim Hellberg’s men, with Dael Fry powering in a header on 25 minutes.

But Millwall battled back after the break, equalising early in the half before scoring what proved to be the winner with four minutes left.

Boro were unchanged from the 0-0 draw with Blackburn Rovers before the international break, and produced a pulsating first half display to deservedly go in at half-time with the lead.

The first opening came as early as the second minute as Callum Brittain paced down the right and fizzed in a low ball which found Tommy Conway, whose strike was deflected over.

Boro had 11 first half corners and their first two both produced chances, with Alan Browne heading over and Fry volleying an even better opportunity over from close range.

Adilson Malanda headed over from a Brittain free-kick before the right-back had a strike at goal himself which Anthony Patterson saved.

Our deserved breakthrough came on 25 minutes, and again it was a corner which helped produce the goods. Millwall got Brittain’s delivery half-cleared but Aidan Morris kept it alive before teeing up Browne, who swung in a superb cross to the back post, where Fry was on hand to power it home with his head.

David Strelec’s hold-up play caused constant problems to the Millwall back-line and he almost created a quickfire second for Boro. He drove through the centre and played in McGree, whose strike was bravely blocked.

There was a scare at the other end when Mihailo Ivanovic’s shot struck the leg of Malanda and bounced narrowly past the post.

But it was Boro making most of the inroads. Strelec had another effort deflected over after powering inside from the right, and Fry was denied a second when his goalbound shot was brilliantly blocked by Femi Azeez.

There were further sights of goal for Fry and McGree before the break, but Boro went in at it with one goal to show for their dominance and much to build on in the second half.

The Teessiders attempted to do just that in the early stages and there was a quick opening for Matt Targett, but his strike was straight at Ivanovic.

Sol Brynn did brilliantly to keep Boro level at the other end moments afterwards, swiping the ball bravely away after Jake Cooper’s header had deflected against Luke Ayling.

He could do nothing to prevent the equaliser on 58 minutes, though, as Josh Coburn’s strike from inside the six-yard box had just too much on it for the goalkeeper.

The game was now stretched, with openings at both ends. Azeez drew a sharp save from Brynn after cutting inside from the right as Millwall looked for a quickfire double, and Ayling produced a block from Zak Sturge.

Boro attempted to get back on top and could have gone back in front when Brittain’s free-kick whistled towards the roof of the net, only for Patterson to tip it over. Ayling’s header from the resulting corner deflected into the side netting.

There was almost an opening on the break when Conway drove through the centre and conjured a shooting position, but his strike was blocked.

Morris was another to be denied by a block after a ball across from McGree but the crucial second just would not come for Boro, who were then hit by a sucker punch at the other end.

Coburn was again the man for the Lions, firing into the bottom corner from the left of the area with four minutes remaining.

An early chance for an equaliser fell to McGree, whose strike from the right of the box was deflected wide.

There was to be no leveller for Hellberg's side, though, with McGree twice denied in the closing stages as Millwall took the points.

Boro are back in action on Monday, away to Swansea City.

Tommy Conway’s second half penalty earned Boro a share of the spoils in a topsy-turvy encounter away to Swansea City.

An excellent start from Boro was rewarded when Alex Bangura fired in the opener in the 11th minute, but Kim Hellberg’s side were unable to build on that advantage.

A pair of Zan Vipotnik penalties handed Swansea the half-time lead as Boro were handed plenty of work to do after the break.

The Teessiders battled tirelessly in the second half to restore parity, and got their reward with 15 minutes remaining when Conway fired in from the spot.

The game was stretched in the closing stages and Boro looked the more dangerous to win it, but the crucial fifth goal was not forthcoming as it ended level.

Boro started with verve and had plenty of joy down the left before taking the lead with a goal worked down that channel on 11 minutes.

Conway released a scampering Bangura and he rifled into the roof of the net as he marked his return to the team with a stunning strike.

It could have been a quickfire double for the Teessiders when Riley McGree found David Strelec and he carried the ball centrally before seeing a low effort saved by Lawrence Vigouroux.

Swansea responded well, and Bangura was again in the thick of the action as the hosts equalised.

The left-back fouled Liam Cullen in the area and Championship top scorer Vipotnik stepped up to roll his team level from the spot.

Boro looked the likelier of the teams to grab the game’s third goal. Bangura’s cross found McGree, who was denied by a block. There were later strikes from Strelec, Conway and McGree which cannoned against a defender.

Conway guided a Callum Brittain corner wide while at the other end, Luke Ayling blocked from Melker Widell and Vipotnik volleyed over.

The game was now open, with chances at both ends. Boro almost went back in front when a cross from Fin Munroe – brought on for the injured Bangura – found Ayling at the back post, and the defender’s ball across the area narrowly evaded a touch.

It was part of a dramatic period of stoppage time, with Swansea awarded a second penalty wen Sol Brynn was adjudged to have fouled Jisung Eom. Vipotnik again made no mistake from 12 yards, picking out the bottom-left corner.

Munroe had a free-kick beaten away by Vigouroux in the eighth added minute, but Boro went in behind at the break.

The second half required plenty of patience from Boro as Swansea dropped deeper and proved difficult to break down.

We would have been back on level terms just after the hour but for a brilliant save from Vigouroux, who sprung to his left to tip an Aidan Morris curler wide with his fingertips.

Munroe was dangerous down the left and fired wide from the edge of the area as Boro continued to push.

The golden opportunity for an equaliser finally came with 15 minutes left as Brittain weaved between two defenders before being brought down by Eom.

Conway was the man tasked with the responsibility from the spot, and the third penalty taken in front of the Boro supporters was converted as the Scotland international fired down the middle to bring us level.

Boro had the wind in their sails and opportunities came for a winner.

Lively substitute Sontje Hansen fired inches wide from the edge of the area, Adilson Malanda had a shot blocked, Ayling fired over and Alex Gilbert saw a drive saved by Vigouroux.

Brynn had to be alert at the other end, pulling off a superb stop to deny Cullen with three minutes remaining.

Five added minutes did not provide a fifth goal of the game - despite a late chance for Kaly Sene - as it ended all-square.

A last-gasp deflected strike saw Portsmouth take the points at the Riverside.

On a frustrating afternoon, Kim Hellberg's men pushed for a breakthrough throughout, including a second half which saw a number of key chances created.

They were unable to break the deadlock, though, and Pompey scored a dramatic winner seven minutes into second half stoppage time with a strike from Adrian Segecic which deflected against Conor Chaplin on its way in.

Dael Fry replaced Luke Ayling in the starting line-up for Boro, who started well.

Alan Browne went close to putting the Teessiders ahead in the ninth minute after good work down the left by Jeremy Sarmiento, but his low drive was met by a strong one-handed save by Nicolas Schmid.

Moments later, Adilson Malanda had an effort deflected onto the roof of the net as Boro aimed to make their early work count.

We were unable to build on that in terms of chance creation, though, despite dominating possession.

It took until just before stoppage time for Schmid to be threatened again, but his save from Fry’s header was comfortable.

A double half-time change saw Ayling and Sontje Hansen introduced, and Boro began the second half with an added spark.

Within two minutes of the restart, there was a golden chance for the opener as David Strelec’s threaded ball was left by Browne to allow Riley McGree to run onto it, and he saw his low strike blocked by the body of Schmid, who also denied Aidan Morris soon after.

Boro were much more threatening than they had been before the interval, and openings continued to come.

McGree had a shot blocked by Regan Poole, Pompey defender Jordan Williams slid one just past his own post and Strelec headed wide from a Callum Brittain corner.

There was another opportunity midway through the second half when a nicely-worked move ended with Tommy Conway slipping in Browne, whose clipped effort was saved by Schmid.

Browne almost had an even better chance as a corner was helped on by Fry and Ayling towards him at the back post, but the ball was taken off his foot just as he prepared to stab it home.

The resulting corner was half-cleared to McGree, whose excellent strike was tipped over by a sprawling Schmid.

Hansen had a drive saved by Schmid and fellow substitute Alex Gilbert had a strike blocked as the breakthrough continued to elude Boro.

The closest we came was a sweet effort by Hansen as the game ticked into stoppage time, which Andre Dozzell brilliantly cleared off the line with his head.

That proved pivotal, with Portsmouth scoring the winner on 97 minutes as Segecic's volley from outside the area hit Chaplin and went in.

Boro were denied a superb win at Ipswich Town as Jack Clarke struck late on to earn the hosts a share of the spoils.

A resilient Boro side led twice in a pulsating encounter at Portman Road, with David Strelec opening the scoring on 25 minutes after some fine work down the right by Aidan Morris and Alan Browne.

Ipswich quickly hit back through Kasey McAteer but the Teessiders kept battling, and went back in front less than 20 minutes into the second half as Tommy Conway finished from close range.

There were chances for a third but the home team held firm, and netted their second equaliser from the penalty spot on 87 minutes to take a point.

Ipswich went into the game three points ahead of Boro, and although there were few clear-cut opportunities in the early stages, they looked the likelier to make the breakthrough.

The lively Ivan Azon flicked wide at the near post from a McAteer ball and later saw a strike deflected wide off the toe of Dael Fry.

The Tractor Boys went closer still when Jaden Philogene slid a shot wide from another McAteer cross, and less than a minute later, Boro had the advantage.

Morris found Browne down the right and the Republic of Ireland international controlled the ball excellently before putting it on a plate for Strelec, who finished from close range.

Boro’s lead lasted less than five minutes, though. Ipswich worked the ball well down the right and Azon flicked it into the path of McAteer, who punched into the bottom corner from the edge of the area.

Sol Brynn did well to deny Philogene six minutes before the break and Strelec had a half-volley saved at the other end as the teams went in at half-time level.

Boro began the second half brightly, but Ipswich conjured the first chance as Strelec did well to block Marcelino Nunez’s drive.

There was a golden opportunity for the Teessiders to go back in front soon after. Conway released Browne down the right and his ball to the back post was controlled and fired goalwards by Alex Gilbert, who was denied by a combination of the post and Azor Matusiwa on the line.

Strelec had a shot beaten away by Walton while at the other end, Brynn saved excellently from Azon and McAteer flicked wide as he diverted a Jack Taylor effort towards goal.

Boro sent the sold-out away end into raptures on 64 minutes as Hellberg’s men reclaimed the lead. Callum Brittain found Strelec down the right and he did brilliantly to return the favour. The right-back’s strike was saved by the foot of Walton but the ball bounced to Conway, who slid it home from close range.

The Teessiders were buoyant and the advantage could have been extended. Jeremy Sarmiento – brought on against his former club – advanced through the centre and had a shot pushed away by Walton, who also denied Strelec soon after.

Ipswich tried to generate some pressure at the other end but Boro were proving equal to it, with one dangerous move leading to a strike from Anis Mehmeti which Brynn gathered.

The equaliser came from the penalty spot after Adilson Malanda was adjudged to have fouled George Hirst in the box. Clarke stepped up to send Brynn the wrong way and earn his team a share of the spoils.

Morgan Whittaker marked his return to the starting XI with a goal as Boro got the better of Sheffield Wednesday.

Whittaker – making his first start since early March following an injury – pounced on a loose backpass to open the scoring just 11 minutes into the game at the Riverside.

Boro fans expecting a flurry of further goals would be left waiting in vain for a second, with Wednesday proving difficult and spirited opponents.

In the end, one goal was enough for Boro to return to winning ways ahead of the final two games of the regular season.

After few moments of attacking quality at either end in the early stages, the game burst into life in the 11th minute. A ball directed back towards Wednesday goalkeeper Murphy Cooper was latched onto by an alert Whittaker, who touched it past the stopper before rolling calmly into an empty net.

There were numerous openings for the Teessiders to extend that advantage in the remainder of the first half, but Cooper would not be beaten again.

He was twice indebted to defender Gabriel Otegbayo, though, as he brilliantly blocked a goalbound Alan Browne drive with his head before producing another brave interception, keeping out a powerful David Strelec volley.

Cooper pushed a Whittaker drive wide and Dael Fry saw a header cleared off the line by Jerry Yates.

Further chances went to Browne and Whittaker, but neither were able to extend Boro’s lead as the hosts went in at half-time a goal to the good.

Boro were the side enjoying the bulk of the possession but Wednesday’s heads did not drop, despite their challenging season to date.

There were half-openings for Boro in the first 10 minutes of the second half, but Whittaker and Aidan Morris were off-target with their efforts from outside the area.

Luke Ayling forced Cooper into a save from a corner but at the other end, Sol Brynn needed to be alert to save a low shot from substitute Will Grainger.

There were sights of goals at both ends in the closing stages as the game became stretched, but neither goalkeeper was seriously tested again, although Jeremy Sarmiento did beat Cooper with a clip which was cleared off the line.

Boro saw it out to claim maximum points ahead of Saturday's home match against Watford.

Morgan Whittaker was instrumental as Boro extended their automatic promotion hopes with a second successive victory, seeing off Watford in style at the Riverside.

In the final home game of the regular league season, Whittaker put Kim Hellberg’s side into an early lead in style, stroking a free-kick into the top corner from 25 yards.

A dangerous Watford side had opportunities to level but on the stroke of half-time, David Strelec bundled in a second for the Teessiders to seemingly set us on the road to victory.

Watford halved the deficit early in the second half to give themselves some hope, but Whittaker quickly restored the two-goal advantage to calm any nerves.

Substitute Tommy Conway got in on the act with 15 minutes remaining, rattling a penalty into the bottom corner.

And the Scotland international wrapped it up in stoppage time with a ruthless finish in front of the South Stand.

It proved to be a confidence-boosting afternoon for Boro ahead of next weekend’s trip to Wrexham.

A Boro side featuring four changes from the side which started the midweek win over Sheffield Wednesday started brightly.

One of the players brought in, Alex Gilbert, had the first sight of goal with a deflected strike which flew wide.

It was not long until the Riverside was bouncing, though, as Whittaker curled a tremendous free-kick into the top corner from distance for his second goal in as many games.

Watford had plenty of sniffs of an equaliser. Edo Kayembe struck wide from the edge of the box and Luca Kjerrumgaard had a pair of chances, hooking one into the hands of Sol Brynn and firing another narrowly past the post.

Hornets captain Imran Louza also needed to be watched closely. After Boro conceded possession deep inside their own half, the Moroccan curled wide from distance. He also sent a free-kick just off-target from 20 yards.

Their best opening came on 33 minutes when they broke away down the left and Kjerrumgaard motored in behind. His shot across goal looked to be heading for the bottom corner until Brynn got a crucial touch on it to send it crashing into the post.

Boro began to take control again in the closing stages of the half, and warning were fired with efforts from range by Luke Ayling and Callum Brittain.

The reward came in stoppage time when Gilbert released Whittaker down the right of the area before his low cross struck the foot and then head of Strelec as it was bundled over the line.

Boro were well aware of Watford’s continued danger, and that was underlined just three minutes into the second half when they pulled a goal back, with James Abankwah firing in at the back post.

That sparked Hellberg’s men into life, with half-time substitute Matt Targett at the heart of several bright moves.

One of them saw him play in Sontje Hansen with a superb pass, but the Curacao international could only screw the ball wide.

Gilbert created a shooting opportunity for himself before prodding an effort which was saved by Egil Selvik, but the goalkeeper could do nothing to prevent us restoring our two-goal lead in the 58th minute.

Targett was again key, sending in a low ball which Watford failed to get clear. Whittaker pounced from close range to double his tally for the afternoon.

Boro were now playing with great confidence and had a fourth goal in their sights.

Strelec rattled a shot against the legs of Selvik and Whittaker deserved a hat-trick with a piledriver of a strike from distance which rifled against the underside of the bar. It was among his last actions before being brought off to a standing ovation.

Two of the players brought on as part of that change – Conway and Leo Castledine – combined to great effect on 71 minutes. Conway teed up Castledine on the edge of the box and his sweet hit was well-saved by Selvik.

Moments after, Conway had an opportunity himself as he sprinted through the centre, but a fine block denied him.

The Scotland international got the goal he had been threatening with 15 minutes left, firing a penalty into the bottom corner after a clear handball in the area by Abankwah.

Boro continued to dominated the game's closing stages, but a fifth goal eluded the hosts until two minutes into stoppage time as Strelec released Conway and he dispatched a strike into the bottom corner.

It was a superb afternoon for Hellberg's side, who wrap up the regular league season away to Wrexham next Saturday.

Boro’s regular season ended with a pulsating draw which confirmed the Teessiders’ play-off fate, while also denying opponents Wrexham’s path into the top six.

Tommy Conway and David Strelec continued their good form with a goal apiece as Boro claimed a point - one which sets up a two-legged play-off semi-final against Southampton.

Boro’s slim ambitions of automatic promotion were all but extinguished as Ipswich Town raced into a two-goal lead elsewhere, but Wrexham’s hopes ebbed and flowed throughout the day as they played out a tense three-way battle with Derby County and eventual victors Hull City. 

Hellberg’s side made the perfect start in North Wales when, with less than five minutes on the clock, Tommy Conway made the breakthrough. Callum Brittain showed great endeavour down the right flank before delivering into the area where Boro’s number 9 forced home his third goal in two games. 

Wrexham, themselves chasing the Championship’s final play-off place, were never going to go quietly - and the hosts struck next. 

A cheaply-conceded free-kick from Boro proved costly, as Josh Windass stepped up to curl home an unstoppable effort past Sol Brynn. 

With the scores level, Boro enjoyed their best spell of the half, but a second goal proved elusive. Conway’s dangerous ball into the box escasped every blue and black shirt, then minutes later a goalmouth scramble ended in Wrexham keeper Danny Ward gratefully grasping the ball. 

Then, Wrexham broke at the other end to take the lead for the first time in the contest, Issa Kabore getting to the byline and delivering an inviting cross which Sam Smith stooped to head home. 

Boro, though, found an immediate response when David Strelec connected with Matt Targett’s flighted ball from the left to steer past Ward and restore parity. 

A half-time change from Hellberg saw the return of Riley McGree from a brief injury hiatus; he replaced Alan Browne.

The early stages of the second period brought opportunities at either end. Smith poked high to force a save from Brynn, and Ollie Rathbone stung the palms of the Boro keeper with another effort. 

For Boro, Conway jinked his way into a promising area from wide but couldn’t pick out a teammate, and sub McGree had a strike blocked at the end of an enterprising run.

The Teessiders freshened things up further with the introduction of Jeremy Sarmiento and Leo Castledine, and the latter could have netted with his first touch when picked out by Conway - he showed good feet to work space, but was denied by Ward at point-blank range. Soon after, Luke Ayling glanced a header inches wide of the far post from a Targett free-kick.

Results elsewhere began to turn against the hosts, and they became increasingly forward-thinking. They raced forward after clearing a Boro corner, their substitute Nathan Broadhead leading the charge before pulling back to Windass who slammed over.

The Red Dragons piled on the pressure as they chased what for them would be a vital winner, but Boro held firm to end the regular season with a point.

Boro’s playoff semi-final with Southampton is finely poised after a gripping goalless draw in the first leg at the Riverside.

The Teessiders thoroughly dominated the first half, and Southampton turned the screw in the second. Both sides hit the woodwork - but ultimately, nothing separates the sides as we head to the south coast on Tuesday.

In the build-up, thousands of home fans lined the surrounding streets to greet the team bus as it made its way into the Riverside, creating a cacophony of noise and colour to welcome the Boro and add further edge to proceedings.

Settling quickly into the two-legged tie, Boro were the first to carve open a series of half-chances; Riley McGree with the most promising as he poked narrowly wide from Callum Brittain’s low ball across goal.

Luke Ayling was next to go close when he tiptoed through a few challenges and arrowed a vicious strike narrowly wide.

Tommy Conway had Boro’s best opportunities of a dominant first half - the first was a close-range shot which was kept out by an incredible block from Saints’ James Bree, then our number nine struck the base of the post at the end of a quick breakaway after being laid on by McGree.

Boro kept up the intensity in the first half's closing stages, and had further chances still; the home fans were left wondering how the ball hadn’t found its way over the line when Morgan Whittaker’s corner caused bedlam in the visitors’ box.

Southampton, who must have been somewhat shellshocked by such a one-sided opening 45, reemerged looking determined to make more of a contest of it. Their best chance to that point arrived early in the second period when Cyle Larin headed Tom Fellows’ cross wide. Larin was soon to be replaced by Ross Stewart up top, while Saints also introduced Shea Charles and Kuryu Matsuki.

Kim Hellberg made a switch of his own, as McGree made way for Alan Browne in the middle of the park. Soon after, Leo Castledine and Jeremy Sarmiento were on the field too, in place of Strelec and Whittaker.

As the battle wore on, the visitors began to show some of the form that has led to their lengthy unbeaten run in the second half of the league campaign. 

Taylor Harwood-Bellis hammered a header against the crossbar following a free-kick, and Samuel Edozie dragged wide at the end of one particularly dangerous counter.

Neither side could make the breakthrough though, and it's firmly in the balance as we look ahead to 90 more minutes between the sides on Saints territory next Tuesday.

An extra time goal from Southampton edged a blood and thunder play-off semi-final with Boro at St Mary’s.

Having battled it out over 180 minutes of normal time in the two legs, it was in the final 15 that Saints dealt a brutal final blow.

With an unchanged XI from the weekend’s goalless draw at the Riverside, Boro made the perfect start at St Mary’s with the lead inside the first five minutes. 

Kim Hellberg’s side had been knocking the ball about nicely, and there were shouts for an early penalty when a stray boot caught David Strelec in Saints territory.

Undeterred, Boro kept going and when Callum Brittain found space to advance down the right, he teased a pass into the path of Riley McGree who swept expertly into the bottom corner. It was Boro’s first goal in a play-off match after five previous blanks, and well deserved for an enterprising start on the south coast.

The Teessiders were soon in the hunt for a second, too, and Morgan Whittaker was unlucky when he twisted and turned past Ryan Manning and curled into the side netting.

The Saints remained a threat though, and there was a sigh of relief for Boro when Ross Stewart prodded Manning’s clever cross back across goal and wide.

The contest became increasingly stop-start, and while Boro were content to try and contain, as time wore on the heat and intensity was slowly cranked up by the hosts and their fans. Boro’s superb travelling army, in fine voice throughout, responded in kind to lift their team.

Set pieces appeared to be a key weapon in the Saints armoury, and it was in first half stoppage time that the home side took advantage when - after a superb save from Sol Brynn to keep the ball out from Manning’s back post volley, Stewart rose highest to nod home the loose ball and level things up.

As with the first half, the second began with Boro enjoying a spell on the ball and once more there were penalty appeals from the blue and black shirts - this time for handball - which were waved away. 

Southampton continued to apply the pressure with dead balls, and Boro did well to clear one deep corner from danger before Manning’s smart turn and shot flicked narrowly wide off Luke Ayling.

After his first half goal, the physical presence off Stewart was ever a danger - he got the better of Dael Fry on one occasion and laid wide to Leo Scienza, but Ayling did well to marshal away the danger as the Saints man hit the deck.

Next it was Boro’s turn to threaten from a set play - Matt Targett’s free-kick found Fry in all sorts of space, but his header back across goal was well dealt with. 

Minutes later, Whittaker unleashed a fierce drive at the end of a counter attack having been picked out by McGree, but it zipped wide off a red and white shirt.

With twenty minutes left on the clock, Boro were forced into a first change of the evening as Tommy Conway hobbled off to be replaced by Alan Browne. For the hosts, Flynn Downes was on for Kuryu Matsuki.

Further changes as we entered the final ten saw Leo Castledine on for Strelec, and Southampton responded with Cyle Larin and Samuel Edozie replacing Stewart and Scienza.

Substitute Larin stung the palms of Sol Brynn as Saints capitalised on a loose touch as the clock ticked into five minutes of stoppage time, but the Boro stopper did well to push it away. Larin had the home crowd on their feet appealing for a penalty soon after following a collision with Fry, but replays showed Fry had come off worse in the coming together. The Boro skipper soldiered on.

That was that for the 90 minutes, and with nothing to separate the teams, 30 more were on the way.

The first half of it saw very little in the way of goalmouth action. Tiring Boro stuck to their task, and continued to dig in with blocks, tackles and clearances.

One fresh face was introduced for the second 15 of extra time, with Jeremy Sarmiento allowing goalscorer McGree to take a well-earned reprieve.

It was in those final stages, though, that the Saints delivered the fatal blow. After Boro had twice half-cleared their lines, Shea Charles shaped to deliver another ball into the area which floated all the way through Boro’s lines and nestled in the bottom corner.

Keeper Brynn was twice thrown into the mix as Boro desperately sought a late equaliser, but to no avail as the Saints claimed the victory.

Boro tasted Wembley heartbreak again as Oli McBurnie’s injury-time winner ended our season in the cruelest fashion.

A tense, dogged 100-minute affair between two sides giving everything in roasting temperatures was settled at the last when the Tigers striker found the net to deny Boro promotion to the Premier League.

After setting up camp in impressive style at Trafalgar Square on Friday evening, more than 36,000 Boro fans streamed down Wembley Way on Saturday in searing sunshine.

There was one change to Kim Hellberg’s XI from the side that had travelled to Southampton in the semi-final second leg; Tommy Conway, who picked up an injury on the south coast, was replaced by Alan Browne. The substitutes’ bench brought a welcome addition to Boro’s roster, with Hayden Hackney included for the first time since his lay-off in mid-March.

Hull, meanwhile, included a number of familiar faces in their ranks - former Boro duo Ryan Giles and Matt Crooks both started, while Paddy McNair made the bench.

Temperatures continued to climb as the contest got underway, and Boro set the early tempo. Matt Targett’s low cross from the left was an inviting one for David Strelec to attack, but the Tigers got a toe on the ball first.

Boro were enjoying the lion’s share of possession, and Strelec went close again when his header from Alan Browne’s delivery looped wide. 

At the other end, Sol Brynn was called into action for the first time to tip over a Lewie Coyle header which may have been on its way over anyway. Mohamed Belloumi then set his sights from distance with a whipped effort that flew wide. 

The first half’s dying embers produced the closest chances for both sides. 

First, it was Hull’s turn to go close as Giles’ cross picked out McBurnie whose header glanced the woodwork on its way over.

Then, in front of the Boro supporters, Morgan Whittaker and Strelec linked up from a long ball over the top before the latter arrowed a strike narrowly past the far post.

Boro were back in control at the start of the second period. 

Strelec charged down Ivor Pandur’s clearances and was unlucky that the ricochet flew away from danger. Minutes later, Riley McGree headed down Luke Ayling’s flighted pass for Whittaker to hit with venom - it was well blocked.

Skipper Dael Fry went closer still from the resulting corner, his back-post header landed on the roof of the City net.

The biggest roar yet from the red half of Wembley came when Hackney got stripped and ready for his introduction to the battle. He replaced Strelec with around twenty minutes to play.

The Teessiders were then forced into another change within minutes, as McGree pulled up - the Australian visibly distraught to leave the field as Sontje Hansen took his place.

The two subs combined to get the Boro fans on their feet, Hackney poking through to Hansen who was kept out by an excellent Ivor Pander save - the offside flag then went up, but neither side were to know that.

Back in Boro territory, Hull’s own sub Joe Geldhart produced a smart swivel and shot but couldn’t find the target. 

The game looked set for extra time with both sides struggling to carve out openings, but it was into eight minutes of added time that Hull struck the killing blow. A ball in from the left from Yu Hirakawa was parried loose by Brynn, and McBurnie was on hand to stab home the telling goal.
